L431: ## Analysis Populations
L432: ## **The ITT Population**
L433: Included all randomized subjects, analyzed according to the treatment they were randomized to receive, and if different, not according to what they actually received.
L434: ## **The Microbiological ITT Population**
L435: Was the subset of subjects in the ITT population who had causative (i.e., infecting) pathogens identified by the central microbiology laboratory from skin lesion or blood cultures; local laboratory identification results were only used if the corresponding causative pathogen was not available for identification by the central laboratory. Subjects with no pathogens isolated at Baseline (microbiologically non-evaluable) were excluded from the microbiological ITT (micro-ITT) population.
L436: ## **CE Population**
L437: Was the subset of subjects in the ITT population who complied with important aspects of the trial until the TOC visit, i.e., with no major protocol deviations (e.g., a completed response outcome assessment, and no concomitant systemic antibacterial treatment or topical antibacterial applied to the primary lesion).
L438: ## **The Microbiologically Evaluable Population**
L439: Was the subset of subjects in the micro-ITT population who were also in the CE population. Analysis at each time point was performed on subjects with available response at that time point (excluding those with microbiological response of 'Not Evaluable' or missing).
L440: ## Sample Size Determination
L441: A sample size of 674 subjects (337 per arm) provided at least 90% power to reject the null hypothesis (H0) against the alternative hypothesis (HA) at the one-sided alpha level of 0.025 as follows, using a two-arm large-sample normal approximation test of Proportions. Early clinical response rates of an at least 20% reduction in lesion area size (primary endpoint) and clinical cure rates at the TOC visit (main secondary endpoint) were based on recent phase 3 studies in ABSSSI. The sample size estimate was based on a point estimate for early clinical response of 80% in each treatment arm in the ITT and CE population, a one-sided alpha level of 0.025, a non-inferiority margin of 10 percentage points for the between-arm difference of the primary endpoint.
L442: ## Data Monitoring and Interim Analyses
L443: Investigators, Applicant employees, and others involved in the conduct and analysis of the Trial (with the exception of the unblinded pharmacist or delegate) remained blinded to the treatment codes and interim analysis results until all monitoring decisions were made, and the database locked for the final analysis.
L444: A blinded interim analysis for sample size re-estimation assessed whether the initial sample size estimate was adequate for evaluating the primary endpoint, and to select a larger sample size if warranted.
L445: NDA 218275
Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
L446: The blinded interim analysis was performed in November 2018, and was based on pooled information across the two treatment arms when early clinical response data were available for 60% of the subjects planned to be randomized (approximately 404 subjects). The number and percentage of responders and non-responders based on the primary Endpoint (and Clinical Success / No-Success based on the main secondary endpoint) were provided.
L447: ## **Reviewer Comments:**
L448: *The interim analyses appeared to be conducted appropriately and there were no major concerns. Note that no statistical adjustment was required, and the sample size specified in the protocol remained unchanged after the blinded review of the primary and secondary endpoints.*
L449: ## **Statistical Methods**
L450: Trial BPR-CS-008 was designed to determine whether ceftobiprole was non-inferior to vancomycin plus aztreonam for both the primary endpoint of early clinical response and the main secondary endpoint of investigator-assessed clinical success at the TOC visit. The main primary analysis was based on the ITT population consisting of all randomized subjects. The weighted difference in percentage of responders at 48–72 h (ceftobiprole arm minus the vancomycin plus aztreonam arm), and the 95% CI for the weighted difference was computed using CMH weights method adjusted for geographical region (North America and Europe), and actual type of ABSSSI.
L451: The non-inferiority hypothesis test was a one-sided hypothesis test performed at the 2.5% level of significance. If the lower limit of the two-sided 95% CI for the difference in response rates (ceftobiprole minus vancomycin plus aztreonam) in the ITT population was greater than -10%, the non-inferiority of ceftobiprole to vancomycin plus aztreonam would be concluded. If non-inferiority was declared at the one-sided significance level of 0.025, then the difference would be tested for superiority. Superiority would be declared if the lower limit of the two-sided 95% CI exceeded 0 (or equivalently p-value less than 0.05 using CMH test). The same analysis was repeated on the CE population.
L452: ## **Reviewer Comments**
L453: *The overall data from two studies by Snodgrass in 1937, both of which compared ultraviolet light against a sulfonamide antibacterial drug, in subjects with cellulitis/erysipelas for an outcome of cessation of spread of lesion at 48-72 hours, support a treatment difference of 18%. Because this is thought to be conservatively estimated at 18 percent for antibacterial drugs in the treatment of ABSSSI for the endpoint based on lesion size assessment, further discounting of the treatment effect may not be necessary and thus M1 is estimated to be 18 percent. These scientific data provide support for the selection of a noninferiority margin of 10 percent that preserves some of M1 based on an endpoint of lesion size assessment. Refer to the ABSSSI Guidance2 for further details on the justification of a 10% NI margin for ABSSSI.*
L454: *The main secondary analysis was based on the weighted difference in percentage of clinical success at the TOC visit (ceftobiprole arm minus the vancomycin plus aztreonam arm), and the*

L457: 95% CI for the weighted difference was computed using CMH weights method, adjusted for geographical region (North America and Europe), and actual type of ABSSSI.
L458: Superiority would be declared if the lower limit of the two-sided 95% CI exceeds 0 (or equivalently p value less than 0.05 using CMH test).
L459: ## 6.2.2.4. Results of Analyses, Trial BPR-CS-008
L460: ## Primary Analysis
L461: As shown in Table 27, ceftobiprole met the primary objective of this trial by demonstrating the non-inferiority of ceftobiprole (greater than the pre-specified 10% non-inferiority margin) to vancomycin plus aztreonam for the primary endpoint of early clinical response based on a 20% or more reduction from baseline in lesion size at 48–72 hours after start of trial drug administration. In the ITT population (primary analysis population), 306 subjects (91.3%) in the ceftobiprole arm were responders (95% CI: 87.8, 94.1) versus 303 (88.1%) subjects in the vancomycin plus aztreonam arm (95% CI: 84.2, 91.3). The proportion difference (ceftobiprole minus vancomycin plus aztreonam) was 3.3% (95% CI: -1.2, 7.8). Since -1.2% (the lower limit of this 95% CI) exceeded the required NI limit of -10%, non-inferiority was demonstrated.
L462: There were 29 (8.7%) and 41 (11.9%) non-responders in the ceftobiprole and vancomycin plus aztreonam arms, respectively. The most common reason for non-responders at 48–72 hours after start of treatment was &lt;20% reduction from baseline in surface area of primary lesion which included 65.5% of ceftobiprole non-responders and 70.7% of vancomycin plus aztreonam non-responders. In general, there were no notable treatment differences regarding the reasons for non-response.

L469: ## **Secondary Analyses**
L470: As shown in **Table 28**, the main secondary endpoint was also supportive of non-inferiority in the primary analysis. The proportion of clinical successes at TOC was slightly higher in the ceftobiprole arm versus vancomycin plus aztreonam arm, 302/335 (90.1%) versus 306/344 (89.0%), respectively. The proportion difference (ceftobiprole minus vancomycin plus aztreonam) was 1.0% (95% CI: -3.5, 5.6). There were no concerns related to reasons for nonclinical success which were mostly comparable between arms.
L471: There were 33 (9.9%) and 38 (11.0%) nonclinical successes at TOC in the ceftobiprole and vancomycin plus aztreonam arms, respectively. The most common reason for nonclinical success was 'Missing assessment at TOC' which occurred in 60.6% of ceftobiprole non-successes and 60.5% of vancomycin plus aztreonam non-successes. In general, there were no notable treatment differences regarding the reasons for non-success. A slightly greater proportion of subjects in the vancomycin plus aztreonam arm were non-successes due to 'Unplanned surgical procedure for the ABSSSI after start of therapy and prior to TOC' (13.2% versus 6.1%) and there were 2 (5.2%) of non-successes due to 'death prior to TOC' in the vancomycin plus aztreonam arm versus 0 (0.0%) in the ceftobiprole arm.

L515: ## Conclusions
L516: Trial BPR-CS-008 met its primary objective of demonstrating non-inferiority for the primary endpoint. In general, primary and secondary efficacy findings tended to numerically favor ceftobiprole to vancomycin plus aztreonam. Early clinical response appeared to be sustained at later timepoints. Overall, there are no major concerns with the evidence of effectiveness.
L517: Minor concerns were that over 95% of subjects in the ITT population were White, which may limit the generalizability of findings to other races. (b) (4)
L518: ## 6.2.3. CABP, Trial CAP-3001
L519: ## 6.2.3.1. Design, Trial CAP-3001
L520: This was a randomized, double-blind, multicenter trial of ceftobiprole versus ceftriaxone with or without linezolid designed to assess the efficacy and safety of ceftobiprole in adult subjects with CABP requiring hospitalization. The trial was conducted from June 2006 to July 2007.
L521: ## NDA 218275
## Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
L522: The primary objective of this trial was to demonstrate the noninferiority of ceftobiprole compared with ceftriaxone with or without linezolid with respect to the clinical cure rate at the TOC visit in subjects hospitalized with CABP.
L523: The secondary objectives were to compare the following in hospitalized CABP subjects after treatment with ceftobiprole versus treatment with the comparator:
L524: - The microbiological eradication rate at the TOC Visit
- The clinical cure rate and the microbiological eradication rate at the TOC Visit of subjects who required mechanical ventilation within the first 48 hours of enrollment
- The clinical and microbiological relapse rates at the late follow-up visit
- The 30-day pneumonia-specific mortality rates.
L525: Since many subjects in this trial would not require hospitalization for the entire duration of antibacterial therapy, a switch from IV study drugs to oral cefuroxime axetil (500 mg every 12 hours) was allowed after a minimum of 3 days of IV therapy, but only for those subjects who met all protocol-specified criteria for improvement and were candidates for hospital discharge. The use of cefuroxime axetil was consistent with the recommendation of practice guidelines.
L526: All subjects continued to receive intravenous therapy while hospitalized and trial sites were encouraged to keep subjects on IV therapy as long as appropriate in order to maximize the number of subjects receiving a full course of IV study medication. In addition, subjects with a positive blood culture at baseline were required to receive IV study drug for a minimum of 5 days pending results of repeat blood cultures.
L527: The total duration of study drug therapy (IV plus oral) for all subjects was a minimum of 5 days and a target of 7 days. If in the investigator's opinion a subject required additional days of study therapy, the duration of the therapy could have been extended up to a maximum of 10 days. Therapy could have been further extended to a maximum of 14 days.
L528: At the discretion of the investigator, subjects were allowed to receive study drug infusions as outpatients or through a home-care agency, provided they met all other protocol requirements, but all IV study drug infusions had to be administered and monitored by a qualified nurse, a qualified member of the trial staff, or an infusion specialist. No concomitant administration of antibacterial treatments was permitted. The treatment and follow-up schedules are summarized in
L529: Figure 4.
L530: ## NDA 218275
## Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)

L539: An independent data monitoring committee (IDMC) was established to monitor data on an ongoing basis to ensure the continuing safety of subjects enrolled in this trial and the efficacy of
L540: the study drug. The IDMC included independent experts, not affiliated with the Applicant, in internal medicine, critical care medicine, infectious diseases, and biostatistics. The IDMC could call upon experts in other specialties to attend IDMC meetings to provide information regarding unanticipated findings or issues. The committee met on 3 occasions (14 October 2006, 23 January 2007, and 24 May 2007) to review data collected in this Trial and made recommendations after each review to continue conduct of the trial as planned.
L541: ## 6.2.3.2. Eligibility Criteria, Trial CAP-3001
L542: Approximately 670 subjects hospitalized with CABP severe enough to require treatment with IV antibacterials for at least 3 days, were to be enrolled to achieve 532 (266 in each treatment arm) clinically evaluable subjects. In total, 666 subjects at 103 sites worldwide were randomly assigned centrally in a 1:1 ratio to treatment with either ceftobiprole (500 mg every 8 hours as a 120-minute IV infusion) or ceftriaxone (2 g once daily as a 30-minute IV infusion) with or without linezolid (600 mg every 12 hours as a 60-minute IV infusion). Subjects were stratified by the Pneumonia Outcomes Research Team (PORT) Severity Index (PSI) score at randomization (PSI \le 90 versus PSI \ge 91), and by the need for anti-staphylococcal therapy (linezolid or placebo) based on signs, symptoms, and medical history at enrollment.
L543: ## **Inclusion Criteria**
L544: Subjects meeting all the following:
L545: - Men or women, 18 years of age or older who provided written informed consent.
- Women must have been postmenopausal (for at least 1 year), surgically sterile or practiced an effective method of birth control.
- Subjects had a diagnosis of CABP severe enough to require hospitalization and treatment with IV antibacterial drugs for at least 3 days (72 hours), defined as meeting all the following criteria:
- Subjects had a diagnosis of CABP severe enough to require hospitalization and treatment with IV antibacterials for at least 3 days (72 hours), defined as meeting all of the following criteria (must meet a, b, c, d, and e):Clinical diagnosis of acute bacterial pneumonia acquired in the community. Subjects must have resided in the community (i.e., not in a chronic care facility such as a nursing home or rehabilitation facility) and must not have been hospitalized during the 14 days before the onset of symptoms of pneumonia. Residence in an assisted-living facility where the subject had regular access to the community was allowed.
- Clinical signs or symptoms of acute bacterial pneumonia with at least 2 of the following criteria:Cough (new or increased over usual state)
- Production of purulent sputum or a worsening in the character of sputum
- Auscultatory findings on pulmonary examination of rales or evidence of pulmonary consolidation (dullness on percussion, bronchial breath sounds, or egophony)
- Dyspnea or tachypnea (respiratory rate \ge 20 breaths per minute), that was new or worse than usual state
- New onset hypoxemia on room air (PO_2 &lt; 60 mm Hg on arterial blood gas or O_2 saturation &lt; 90\% by pulse oximetry), or respiratory failure that required mechanical ventilation.
- New radiographic infiltrates (not related to another disease process) consistent with the diagnosis of bacterial pneumonia
- Fever or leukocytosis/leukopenia (temporally associated with the onset of pneumonia symptoms)Fever (in the absence of antipyretics) defined as an axillary temperature &gt; 37.5^\circ C, an oral temperature &gt; 38^\circ C, a tympanic temperature &gt; 38.5^\circ C, a rectal temperature &gt; 39^\circ C, or hypothermia, defined as a rectal body temperature of &lt; 35^\circ C
- Leukocytosis defined as an elevated total peripheral WBC count \ge 10 \times 10^9/L or \ge 15\% immature neutrophils (bands), regardless of total peripheral white count; or leukopenia with total WBC \le 4.5 \times 10^9/L
- Severity of pneumonia required IV antibacterial therapy
L546: ## 6.2.3.3. Statistical Analysis Plan, Trial CAP-3001
L547: ## Disposition of Subjects
L548: A total of 706 subjects were enrolled into this trial, Figure 5. Sixty-eight subjects were not included in the ITT analysis set (i.e., the ITT population of all randomized subjects) including 40 subjects who were screen failures and 28 subjects who were randomly assigned to treatment with ceftobiprole (14 subjects) or ceftriaxone with or without linezolid (14 subjects) at site 5060023. A total of 638 subjects were randomized to receive either the ceftobiprole (n = 314) or ceftriaxone with or without linezolid (n = 324) treatment.
L549: One subject was randomly assigned to the comparator arm but was treated with ceftobiprole.
L550: As shown in Table 32, a total of 532 of 638 (83%) of ITT subjects completed the study. Of the 17% of subjects who discontinued the study, the main reasons for study discontinuation were subjects having AEs (5%) or being lost to follow-up (3%). Overall, there were no notable imbalances between the treatment arms regarding reasons for discontinuation from the study.

L561: ## **Baseline Demographic and Disease Characteristics**
L562: As shown in Table 33, the baseline demographic characteristics in the ITT population were generally balanced across the treatment arms. Overall, subjects had a median age of 56 years and tended to be males (57%), White (62%) or not Hispanic or Latino (75%). Approximately 13% of subjects were from North American sites and 41% were from European sites. Disease characteristics were also balanced across the treatment arms. Overall, 22% of subjects had a PSI \ge 91, 49% had a PORT Risk Class of \ge III and 54% had systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) at baseline. Concomitant use of linezolid was observed in 11% of subjects. The percentage of ITT subjects with a valid pathogen at baseline was 29%.

L568: ## **Sample Size Determination**
L569: The sample size was determined to show the noninferiority of ceftobiprole compared with ceftriaxone with or without linezolid in terms of the clinical cure rate at the TOC visit. The sample size calculation was based on the following assumptions for the ITT analysis set:
L570: - The clinical cure rate is 70% in both treatment arms,
- The non-inferiority margin is 10%,
- The power (1-\beta) is 80%,
- The level of significance is 2-sided 5%,
- The clinically evaluable rate is 80%.
L571: Based on the above, 670 subjects needed to be randomly assigned to treatment, providing 335 subjects in each treatment arm.
L572: ## **Efficacy Analysis Sets**
L573: - **ITT Analysis Set:** included all subjects randomly assigned to treatment.
- **mITT Analysis Set:** a subset of the ITT analysis set that included all ITT subjects who had a valid pathogen at Baseline.
- **Clinically Evaluable Analysis Set:** a subset of the ITT analysis set that included all the ITT subjects who received at least 48 hours of Trial medication but excluded those subjects with a derived clinical outcome of Not Evaluable at the TOC Visit. The derived clinical outcome was based on clinical assessment and evaluability of a subject, whereas the clinical outcome collected in the electronic case report form was based on the investigator's assessment.
- **Clinically Evaluable Analysis Set at the Late Follow-Up Visit:** included all clinically evaluable subjects with a derived clinical outcome of cure at the TOC visit and who were clinically evaluable at the late follow-up visit.
- **Microbiologically Evaluable Analysis Set:** a subset of the mITT analysis set that included all mITT subjects who were also clinically evaluable subjects, excluding those with a microbiological outcome of 'Not Evaluable' at the TOC Visit.
- **Microbiologically Evaluable Analysis Set at the Late Follow-Up Visit:** included all microbiologically evaluable subjects with a microbiological outcome of eradication or presumed eradication at the TOC visit and who were microbiologically evaluable at the late follow-up visit.
- **Safety Analysis Set:** The safety analysis set is a subset of the ITT analysis set and included all the subjects in the ITT analysis set who were exposed to any Trial medication.
L574: ## **Derived Clinical Outcome at the TOC Visit**
L575: In the ITT and mITT analyses subjects whose clinical outcomes were assessed as 'Not Evaluable' by the investigator were considered failures. Subjects who were considered clinically cured by the investigator at the TOC Visit but received effective concomitant therapy for any reason, were also considered failures in the ITT and mITT analyses.
L576: ## Cure
L577: A subject was considered a ‘derived clinical cure’ at the TOC visit if the clinical outcome at the TOC visit was cure and the subject was not a ‘derived failure’ as defined below.
L578: ## Failure
L579: A subject was considered a clinical failure at TOC if he or she took study medication for at least 48 hours and met any of the following criteria:
L580: - Clinical outcome at the TOC visit was failure
- Subject withdrew from the treatment because of a treatment-related adverse event
- Subject died due to pneumonia after 48 hours of treatment
- Subject withdrew from the Trial due to lack of efficacy
- Subject missed a TOC visit assessment and the final clinical assessment before the TOC visit was ‘Unchanged’ or ‘Worsened from Baseline’,
- Subject received non-study systemic antibiotics for treatment of pneumonia prior to the TOC Visit.
L581: Subjects who withdrew from treatment because of an adverse event but received a full course of therapy (5 to 14 days) were regarded as clinical cures if the clinical outcome at the TOC Visit was cure.
L582: ## Non-evaluable
L583: A subject was considered ‘non-evaluable’ at the TOC visit if the following criteria were satisfied:
L584: - Subject did not meet the criteria for cure or failure (as defined above), and
- Subject had missing TOC visit or the investigator’s assessment of the clinical outcome at the TOC visit was ‘Not Evaluable’.
L585: ## **Evaluability at the TOC Visit**
L586: A subject was deemed clinically evaluable at the TOC visit unless he or she met any of the following criteria:
L587: - Clinical Diagnosis Unconfirmed: Per the investigator, the inclusion criterion related to a diagnosis of CABP was not satisfied.
- Community-Acquired Pneumonia Unconfirmed: The baseline infiltrate was not consistent with pneumonia by central x-ray evaluation.
- Mortality:Early Mortality: The subject died within 48 hours after the first infusion.
- Unrelated Mortality: The mortality was unrelated to pneumonia and the last clinical assessment was not worsened, and the subject had no treatment-related adverse event, did not withdraw due to lack of efficacy, and had no TOC visit.
- Effective Concomitant Therapy: The subject took a systemic antibacterial drug (administered for a reason other than CABP), against gram-positive or gram-negative pathogens. Subjects who received a concomitant medication with purely anaerobic (e.g., metronidazole), anti-fungal, or antiviral activity were considered evaluable. Subjects who received non-absorbable antibacterial drugs s (e.g., oral vancomycin, neomycin) or topical antibacterial drugs were also evaluable.
- Other Protocol Violations: The presence of neutropenia (absolute neutrophil count \ge 0.5 \times 10^9/L).
- Resistant to Study Drugs:Subjects whose cultures yielded pathogens resistant to both treatment arms of the trial based on central laboratory results (MIC values \ge 16 \text{ mg/mL}), or
- Subjects who withdrew due to “resistant organism at baseline” based on local laboratory results.
- Inappropriate Clinical Evaluation:The subject did not meet the definition of failure and the TOC visit was not completed 6 to 21 days following the last dose of study drug.
- Course Too Short:The subject took study medication for less than 48 hours, or
- The subject had a clinical outcome of ‘Cure’ at the TOC visit but took study medication for less than 120 hours, or
- The subject took less than 80% of scheduled IV study medication.
- Missing TOC Visit: Subjects who missed the TOC visit and did not meet the definition of cure or failure.
L588: ## **Derived Clinical Outcome at the Late Follow-Up Visit**
L589: ## **Clinical Relapse**
L590: A subject was considered a clinical relapse at the late follow-up visit if the subject was an evaluable cure at the TOC visit and any of the following applied:
L591: - The outcome at the late follow-up visit was relapse, or
- The subject died due to pneumonia prior to the late follow-up visit, or
- The subject took effective concomitant therapy for pneumonia between the TOC visit and the late follow-up visit.
L592: ## **Evaluability at the Late Follow-Up Visit**
L593: A subject was considered clinically evaluable at the late follow-up visit if the following criteria were met:
L594: - The subject was evaluable and had a clinical outcome of cure at the TOC visit.
- The subject did not take effective concomitant therapy for a reason other than pneumonia during the period between the TOC and late follow-up visits, OR the subject took effective concomitant therapy for a reason other than pneumonia and was a clinical relapse at the late follow-up visit.
- The subject had a clinical evaluation at the late follow-up visit or the subject died of pneumonia prior to the late follow-up visit.
L595: ## **Microbiological Outcome at the TOC Visit**
L596: Microbiological outcome at the subject level was not directly collected in the electronic case report form, but was obtained through a combination of the clinical assessment, infection symptoms, and the microbiological assessment at the baseline, TOC, and late follow-up visits. For all subjects with a valid pathogen at baseline, the microbiological outcome at the TOC visit was derived following the mapping shown in Table 34 below.

L603: ## **Microbiological Evaluability at the TOC Visit**
L604: A subject was considered microbiologically evaluable at the TOC visit if the following criteria were met:
L605: - Subject was clinically evaluable at the TOC visit
- Subject had a valid pathogen isolated at baseline. To be considered valid, a pathogen must have met the following isolation criteria:Tracheal aspirate, bronchoalveolar lavage, PBS, or other
- Expectorated samples with less than 10 squamous epithelial cells and greater than 25 leukocytes/lpf.
L606: ## **Primary Efficacy Analysis**
L607: The primary efficacy analysis was performed on the clinically evaluable and the ITT co-primary analysis sets. The primary efficacy endpoint was the clinical cure rate at the TOC visit, defined as the ratio of the number of subjects who had a derived clinical outcome of cure at the TOC visit to the total number of the subjects in the analysis set under consideration.
L608: The hypotheses tested were:
L609: - H0: The clinical cure rate of the ceftobiprole arm is more than 10% inferior to that of the ceftriaxone with or without linezolid arm.
- H1: The clinical cure rate of the ceftobiprole arm is no more than 10% inferior to that of the ceftriaxone with or without linezolid arm.
L610: A 2-sided 95% confidence interval based on the Normal approximation for the difference of two binomial proportions was calculated for the between-treatment difference (ceftobiprole minus ceftriaxone with or without linezolid) at the TOC Visit. Noninferiority of ceftobiprole compared with ceftriaxone with or without linezolid was concluded if the lower limit of this confidence interval was greater than or equal to -10%.
L611: ## **Secondary Efficacy Analyses**
L612: The secondary efficacy endpoints were tested using a step-down hierarchical procedure in the following order:
L613: - microbiological eradication rate at the TOC visit,
- clinical cure rate at the TOC visit for subjects who had a PSI score \ge 91,
- the 30-day pneumonia-specific mortality rates.
L614: The microbiological eradication rate at the TOC Visit was defined as the ratio of the number of subjects with a microbiological outcome of Eradication or Presumed Eradication at the TOC visit to the total number of subjects in the analysis set under consideration at the TOC visit. This analysis was performed on the microbiologically evaluable analysis set.
L615: The clinical cure rate for subjects who had a PSI score \ge 91 was defined as the ratio of the number of subjects with PSI score \ge 91 who had a clinical outcome of cure at the TOC visit to the total number of the subjects with a PSI score \ge 91 in the analysis set under consideration. The analysis of the clinical cure rate for subjects who had a PSI score \ge 91 was performed on the clinically evaluable and ITT analysis sets.
L616: Noninferiority hypotheses similar to the primary hypothesis were tested for the microbiological eradication rate and the clinical response rate in subjects with a PSI score \ge 91.
L617: The 30-day pneumonia-specific mortality rate was defined as the ratio of the number of deaths due to pneumonia to the total number of subjects in the analysis set under consideration. This analysis was performed on the clinically evaluable and ITT analysis sets.
L618: Given the limited sample sizes for these tests, a 15% noninferiority margin was used to test all secondary hypotheses. This was documented prior to database lock, but was not prespecified in the protocol or the analysis plan. The 2-sided 95% confidence interval was computed in the same way as for the primary efficacy analysis.
L619: ## 6.2.3.4. Results of Analyses, Trial CAP-3001
L620: ## Primary Efficacy Analysis
L621: The protocol specified two co-primary endpoints to be analyzed in the primary efficacy analysis, which included the clinical cure rate at the TOC visit in the CE and ITT populations. For both co-primary endpoints, treatment differences were shown to satisfy a 10% NI margin based on the respective lower confidence limits exceeding -10% (Table 35). In the clinically evaluable analysis set, the clinical cure rate at the TOC visit was 86.6% (ceftobiprole) versus 87.4% (comparator), a treatment difference of -0.8% (95% CI: -6.9, 5.3) which indicated NI since the lower bound of -6.9% exceeded a -10% limit. In the ITT analysis set, the clinical cure rate at the TOC visit was 76.4% (ceftobiprole) versus 79.3% (comparator), a treatment difference of -2.9% (95% CI: -9.3, 3.6) which indicated NI since the lower bound of -9.3% exceeded the -10% limit.

L633: ## Reviewer Comments
L634: *The Applicant cannot demonstrate non-inferiority for these endpoints due to uncertainty regarding the NI margin. The specified NI margin for the above secondary endpoints has not been scientifically justified and therefore the interpretation of findings for these endpoints may not be clear unless superiority is shown. These endpoints were therefore considered to be descriptive.*

L663: ## **Conclusions**
L664: Based on findings from the re-analyses which followed the guidelines of the CABP 2020 Guidance, Trial CAP-3001 was considered to provide an adequate level of evidence provided there is support from positive trial findings in the other two indications (SAB and ABSSSI). See Section 6.3.1 for further details on the re-analyses.
L665: There were no other major concerns. Minor concerns related to there being very few subjects from U.S. sites included in the Day 3 mITT population (i.e., 7 subjects in the ceftobiprole arm and 10 in the ceftriaxone arm). In addition, only 3 of these 7 subjects (43%) had an early clinical success compared to 7 of 10 (70%) in the ceftriaxone arm.
L666: ## **6.2.4. Community-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia, Trial BPR-PIP-002**
L667: BPR-PIP-002 was a multicenter, randomized, investigator-blind, active-controlled trial conducted in pediatric subjects ages 3 months to less than 18 years with CABP or HABP requiring hospitalization and treatment with IV antibacterial drugs. The primary objective of this trial was to evaluate the safety of ceftobiprole. The trial was not powered for comparative inferential efficacy analysis, and no efficacy endpoint was identified as primary.
L668: Randomization was stratified by 4 age groups (3 months to &lt;2 years; 2 years to &lt;6 years; 6 years to &lt;12 years; 12 years to &lt;18 years) and by diagnosis of HABP or CABP. Subjects were randomized 2:1 within each group to receive either ceftobiprole or the comparator which was an
L669: ## NDA 218275
## Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
L670: IV standard-of-care cephalosporin with optional antibacterial coverage for MRSA (ceftazidime with or without vancomycin for subjects with HABP; ceftriaxone with or without vancomycin for subjects with CABP) for 7-14 days. Subjects were to receive IV antibacterial treatment for at least 3 days but then could be switched to oral antibacterial drugs if clinical improvement criteria for IV to oral switch were met. Ceftobiprole was administered at a dose of 10-20 mg/kg IV every 8 hours, age-adjusted for dose and infusion duration (maximum daily dose was 1500 mg).
L671: ## **Inclusion criteria included:**
L672: - Male or female aged 3 months to &lt;18 years
- Body weight of \ge 5 kg
- Diagnosis of either CABP or HABP requiring hospitalization and characterized by:Fever (&gt;38.5^\circ\text{C}) or hypothermia (&lt;35^\circ\text{C}), and
- Leukocytosis or leukopenia (relevant to subject age and institutional normal ranges)
- At least two of the following signs or symptoms: cough, lower respiratory tract secretions, auscultatory findings of pneumonia, dyspnea/tachypnea, increased work of breathing (retractions, nasal flaring, or grunting), hypoxemia/oxygen saturation &lt;92\% (on room air)
- Subjects with CAP had to present with \ge 1 of the following conditions:
Admission to an intensive care unit, intermediate care unit, or a unit with the ability to provide constant and close monitoring and care
- Suspected infection with multi-drug resistant pneumococci or MRSA
- History of absent or incomplete pneumococcal vaccination (did not receive all vaccinations as per schedule)
- Recent clinical diagnosis of influenza with exacerbation of fever and respiratory symptoms after initial improvement in the symptoms of acute influenza
- Failure to clinically improve on initial antibiotic therapy for \ge 48 hours and need for antibiotic treatment change
- Oxygen saturation on room air \le 90\%
- New or progressive imaging findings consistent with bacterial pneumonia (e.g., X-ray, ultrasound, or computed tomography)
- Requirement for IV antibacterial treatment for pneumonia
- Sufficient vascular access to receive IV study drug
- Informed consent from the parent(s) or legally acceptable representative(s) to participate in the study, and child's assent, as appropriate
- Female subjects who were not pregnant or breast-feeding and met one of the following conditions:Pre-menarchal, or
- A negative serum or urine pregnancy test and willing to use a highly reliable method of contraception during the study until the last follow-up visit
L673: NDA 218275
Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
L674: ## **Exclusion criteria included:**
L675: - Known resistance of the causative pathogen to ceftobiprole or IV standard-of-care cephalosporin treatment (\pm vancomycin)
- On mechanical ventilation at the time of Screening for &gt;48 hours
- Chest trauma with severe lung contusion or flail chest
- Acute respiratory distress syndrome
- Empyema or lung abscess
- Anatomical bronchial obstruction
- Documented or suspected active or currently treated pulmonary tuberculosis
- Documented or suspected atypical bacterial pneumonia, or viral pneumonia without bacterial superinfection, or need for antibiotic coverage with a macrolide
- Known positive result from a rapid diagnostic test for influenza or respiratory syncytial virus, unless bacterial pneumonia secondary to viral respiratory illness is suspected based on a clinical history of exacerbation of fever and respiratory symptoms after initial improvement in the symptoms of an acute respiratory infection
- Documented or suspected pertussis, chemical pneumonitis (e.g., aspiration of gastric contents, inhalation injury), or cystic fibrosis
- Severe immunodeficiency (human immunodeficiency virus [HIV] infection, or congenital or acquired immunodeficiency syndrome)
- Significant laboratory abnormalities (based on local laboratory results) including:Hematocrit &lt;20%
- Absolute neutrophil count &lt;0.5 x 109/L
- Platelet count &lt;50 x 109/L
- Alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), or total bilirubin &gt;5 x the age-specific upper limit of normal
- Creatinine clearance of &lt;50 mL/min/1.73 m2, or requirement for any form of renal dialysis therapy
- Use of systemic antimicrobial therapy for &gt; 24 hours in the 48 hours before randomization for the current episode of pneumonia. Exception: CAP subjects with failure to clinically improve on initial antibiotic therapy for \ge48 hours and need for antibiotic treatment change (see Inclusion criterion 3).
- History of a previous clinically relevant hypersensitivity or serious adverse reaction to beta-lactam antibiotics or to vancomycin
- Poorly controlled seizure disorder (&gt;1 seizure in the month preceding randomization)
L676: The trial comprised the following phases:
L677: - A pre-dosing screening phase of up to 24 hours
- A treatment phase of 7-14 days
- A post-treatment TOC assessment 7–14 days after the EOT visit
- An last follow-up assessment 28–35 days after the last treatment to monitor relapse of pneumonia and safety
L678: The total duration of the study for each subject was to be approximately 5 to 7 weeks.
L679: NDA 218275
Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
L680: A subject was to be discontinued from study drug if any of the following events occurred:
L681: - No adequate response to the antibiotic treatment within 3 days of treatment
- Need for the use of macrolides concomitant to study drug treatment
- Pregnancy
L682: Additionally, a subject could be discontinued from study drug for the following reasons:
L683: - Adverse event
- Abnormal laboratory value
- Abnormal test procedure result
- Intercurrent illness that prevented or interfered with further administration of treatment
- Death
- Protocol deviation
- Lost to follow-up
- Administrative/logistical reasons
L684: For all subjects who discontinued Trial drug, AE monitoring was to be continued up to and including an last follow-up visit 28–35 days after EOT.
L685: The primary endpoint was analysis of AEs on the first 3 days of Trial treatment, at the EOT, TOC and last follow-up visits, though AEs were assessed for the full study period. Secondary endpoints included clinical response at Day 4 and EOT visits, and clinical cure rates at the TOC and last follow-up visits in the ITT and CE populations, and microbiological eradication rates at the TOC and last follow-up visits. Clinical response was assessed by the blinded investigator at Day 4 and EOT as cured (no signs or symptoms of pneumonia), improved (clinically relevant improvement in signs and symptoms), unchanged (no or minor change from baseline) or worsened (clinically relevant increased in severity of signs and symptoms). Clinical cure was assessed by the blinded investigator at the TOC Visit and defined as signs and symptoms of pneumonia normalized or improved to an extent that further antibiotic therapy was not necessary, and stabilization or improvement of chest X-rays post-baseline if these were available. Pharmacokinetic assessments were also performed.
L686: The Trial population consisted of 138 subjects (94 in the ceftobiprole arm, 44 in the comparator arm), of which 94.7% and 100% respectively, completed Trial treatment. Of the subjects in the ceftobiprole arm, 18 were ages 12 to &lt;18 years old, 27 were 6 to &lt;12 years old, 37 were 2 to &lt;6 years old, and 12 were aged 3 months to &lt;2 years. The majority of subjects (94.2%) had CABP, and only 6 subjects had a pathogen identified at baseline. Subjects with ventilator-associated HABP were excluded from the Trial. The median duration of exposure to IV treatment was similar for the ceftobiprole and comparator arms (6 versus 7 days respectively) as was the median duration of exposure to oral treatment (5 days in each arm).
L687: The clinical response was determined at study Day 4, the EOT visit (7-14 days after randomization), and at the TOC Visit (7-14 days after the EOT visit). The ITT population included all subjects who were randomized.
L688: In the ITT population, the clinical response rates in the ceftobiprole and comparator arms were respectively 95.7% and 93.2% on Day 4 (between-arm difference 2.6% [95% confidence interval CI: 5.5, 14.7]), 96.8% and 100% at the EOT visit (between-arm difference -3.2% [95% CI: -9.1, 5.5]), and 90.4% and 97.7% at the TOC visit (between-arm difference -7.3% [95% CI: -15.7, 3.6]).
L689: Evaluation of safety in Trial BPR-PIP-002 was centered on subjects with CABP as there were only two AEs occurring in 8 subjects with HABP in either treatment arm; neither AE was considered a serious adverse event (SAE).
L690: ## 6.3. Key Efficacy Review Issues
L691: ## 6.3.1. Re-Analysis of Trial CAP-3001
L692: ## Issue
L693: CAP-3001 was conducted prior to the CABP Guidance of 2020 and was not designed to assess an early clinical success endpoint (Day 4) in an appropriate Trial population (e.g., PORT Risk Class \ge III) in which a non-inferiority margin could be scientifically justified. Therefore, the Applicant provided several post-hoc re-analyses which considered new analysis populations, endpoints, and selection criteria which closely followed those outlined in the CABP Guidance4.
L694: ## Background
L695: Since Trial CAP-3001 was conducted from June 2006 to July 2007, i.e., before the current FDA CABP Guidance for Industry was issued in June 2020, the Applicant included CSR Addendum 2 in this NDA submission. Addendum 2 included additional post-hoc analyses that were performed after completion of the original CSR (dated November 3, 2009). These new analyses shown in the tables below were taken directly from Addendum 2 of the CSR. These analyses were critical in assessing the overall evidence obtained from this Trial and the Trial's ability to meet the current recommendations for CABP trials outlined in the FDA Guidance.
L696: The endpoints and Trial populations specified in the re-analysis were similar to those described in the Guidance. The primary endpoint in Trial CAP-3001 was clinical cure at the TOC visit which clearly differed from the endpoint of clinical success at Day 4 stipulated in the current guidance. Therefore, the re-analyses considered an early clinical response endpoint at Day 3 (prior to IV to oral switch) which resembled the Guidance endpoint at Day 4, as shown in Table 39. There were also differences in the Trial populations of CAP-3001 and the Guidance. The Applicant modified the analysis populations to be more consistent with the FDA Guidance. There were also differences between the original entry criteria of CAP-3001 and those outlined in the Guidance are shown in Table 40.
L697: 4 FDA guidance for CABP “Community- Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia: Developing Drugs for Treatment, June 2020” (U.S. Department of Health Human Services) (FDA 2020)
L698: ## **Analysis Populations for the Re-analysis**
L699: In total, four analysis populations were used for the re-analyses using the primary endpoint stipulated in the 2020 FDA CABP guidance:
L700: - The 'Day 3-ITT population' comprised all randomized subjects who had at least two of the following symptoms at baseline: tachypnea, cough, production of purulent sputum, or chest pain. Subjects were analyzed according to the study medication assigned at randomization.
- The Day 3-modified ITT population comprised the subset of subjects in the Day 3-ITT population who met all of the following additional criteria: 1. At least one of new-onset hypoxemia, rales or pulmonary consolidation, and leukocytosis or leukopenia. 2. At least two of fever, hypothermia, hypotension, tachycardia, and tachypnea.
- The Day 3-mITT population was the subset of the Day 3-ITT subjects who had a valid pathogen at baseline.
- The Day 3-modified mITT population was the subset of the Day 3-modified ITT subjects who had a valid pathogen at baseline.
L701: The Baseline demographic and disease characteristics in the 'Day 3-ITT population' and the 'Day 3-modified ITT population' are shown in Table 39.
L702: ## **Primary Efficacy Analysis in Re-analysis**
L703: The re-analysis was performed to determine whether ceftobiprole is non-inferior to ceftriaxone \pm linezolid for the primary endpoint of clinical success at Day 3. Analysis of the primary endpoint was based on the Day 3-ITT population and the Day 3-modified ITT population.
L704: A two-sided 95% confidence interval using the Normal approximation to the difference of two binomial proportions, was calculated for the between-treatment difference (ceftobiprole minus ceftriaxone \pm linezolid) at the TOC Visit.
L705: The result for the primary endpoint of the re-analysis was interpreted in the context of a 12.5% non-inferiority margin, i.e., non-inferiority of ceftobiprole compared with ceftriaxone with or without linezolid was interpreted if the lower limit of this confidence interval was greater than or equal to -12.5%.
L706: The same subgroup analyses were performed for the re-analysis of the primary endpoint in accordance with the 2020 FDA CABP guidance as described for the pre-specified primary endpoint of derived clinical cure at the TOC Visit (CAP-3001 CSR Appendix 2.2.1.1). The exception is the subgroup analysis by oral switch status, as none of the subjects in the Trial had switched to oral therapy at the Day 3 assessment.
L707: ## **Reviewer Comments**
L708: *The 12.5% NI margin mentioned above was chosen by the Applicant to be wider than the 10% NI margin for the original primary analysis to account for additional variability from having to reduce the size of the analysis populations to be consistent with the guidelines for populations specified in the 2020 CABP Guidance. However, since a NI margin of 10% was satisfied in the re-analyses for early clinical success in the Day 3 ITT and Day 3 mITT populations (as discussed later in this section), this change in the margin did not impact conclusions.*
L709: ## **Secondary and other efficacy analyses**
L710: For all secondary and other analysis included in the re-analysis, a two-sided 95% confidence interval using the Normal approximation to the difference of two binomial proportions was calculated for the between-treatment difference (ceftobiprole minus ceftriaxone \pm linezolid). Analyses of the secondary and other endpoints were descriptive with no testing against an interpretative non-inferiority margin.

L727: Approximately 97% (618/638) of CAP-3001 ITT subjects had at least two of the following symptoms at baseline: difficulty breathing, cough, production of purulent sputum, or chest pain; this was required to assess the 2020 FDA CABP guidance primary endpoint of early clinical success. L729: ## Assessment
L730: ## **Baseline Demographic and Disease Characteristics**
L731: Baseline demographic and disease characteristics for Day 3 ITT population and Day 3-modified ITT are shown in Table 41. In the Day 3 ITT population, the median age was 56 years, 62% of subjects were White, 66% were not Hispanic or Latino, 87% were from ex-U.S. sites, 29% had a valid pathogen at baseline, 22% of subjects had PORT Risk Class \ge IV and 31% had SIRS at baseline. Compared to the Day 3 ITT population, the Day 3-modified ITT included older subjects (median age of 67 versus 56 years) and a greater percentage of subjects with PORT Risk Class \ge IV (50% vs. 22%) or SIRS (65% vs. 31%). This would be expected given that the Day 3-modified ITT population excluded a large number of lower risk subjects with PORT Risk Classes of I and II (i.e., approximately 51% of the Day 3 ITT population).
L732: In general, there were no major imbalances between the treatment arms in either of these populations which would raise serious concerns. However, in the Day 3-modified ITT population, a slightly lower percentage of subjects with PORT Risk Class \ge IV observed in the ceftobiprole arm (45% versus 54%).

L748: ## Main Efficacy Results
L749: The main efficacy results of the Applicant's re-analysis are presented in Table 42. For the clinical success at Day 3 endpoint in the Day 3 ITT population, success rates were 71.0% (ceftobiprole) versus 71.1% (ceftriaxone), a treatment difference (ceftobiprole – ceftriaxone) of -0.1% (95% CI: -7.2, 7.1). For the clinical success at Day 3 endpoint in the Day 3 modified-ITT population, success rates were 71.1% (ceftobiprole) versus 67% (ceftriaxone), a treatment difference (ceftobiprole – ceftriaxone) of 4.5% (95% CI: -8.8, 17.7). Treatment differences in these analyses were more favorable than those in the originally specified primary analysis of clinical cure rates at TOC (Table 42). These findings appeared to be consistent with the finding of non-inferiority within a 10% NI margin observed in the original primary analysis.
L750: Findings for other efficacy endpoints also tended to be comparable between the treatment arms and generally consistent with non-inferiority. A notable finding was that in the Day 3-modified ITT population, the 28-day ACM rate was observed to be substantially lower in the ceftobiprole arm (2.1%) compared to the ceftriaxone arm (7.8%) with a treatment difference of -5.7% (95% CI: -11.9, 0.5) which approached nominal significance in favor of the ceftobiprole arm.

L761: ## Subgroup Analysis Results
L762: As shown in Table 43, analyses of subgroups in the re-analysis were limited due to the reduced sample size, especially in the Day 3-modified ITT population. There were no nominally significant comparisons observed in the subgroup analyses conducted in the Day 3-modified ITT population. However, there were some notable findings in this population. For example, ceftobiprole tended to have greater efficacy in more severe cases of CABP. For example, in subjects with PORT classes of \ge IV, response rates at Day 3 were 77.3% (ceftobiprole) versus 61.2% (ceftriaxone) whereas comparisons among subjects with PORT classes of III were 66.2% versus 73.0%, respectively. Subgroup comparisons also favored the ceftobiprole arm in subjects with gram-positive pathogens at baseline (13/18 (72.2%) versus 6/14 (42.9%) with pronounced differences also observed for the Day 3 ITT population.
L763: A more detailed comparison of clinical efficacy in subjects with gram-positive and gram-negative causative pathogens is shown in Table 44. Clinical success rate in infections due to *Streptococcus pneumoniae*, the most commonly isolated pathogen, was higher in the ceftobiprole as compared to ceftriaxone group, 27/33 (81.8%) versus 27/41 (65.9%), respectively. Among gram-negative pathogens, *E. coli*, *K. pneumonia*, *H. influenzae*, and *H. parainfluenzae* occurred in sufficient numbers of subjects across the treatment arms and will be included in the indication for CABP in labeling.

L780: ## **Conclusions**
L781: Trial CAP-3001, as originally designed, met its primary objective. When reviewing this Trial under current FDA guidance recommendations, Trial CAP-3001 was considered to have major limitations. However, although the re-analysis was conducted in a post-hoc manner and involved limited sample sizes, findings appeared to be consistent with the assumption of non-inferiority. Findings in the re-analysis showed that treatment differences tended to favor ceftobiprole when considering an earlier time point (i.e., Day 3) as well as a population that excluded subjects with PORT Risk Classes of 1 or 2 (i.e., Day 3 mITT). Positive findings for the CAP-3001 Trial are considered adequate as evidence of effectiveness for the CABP indication provided they are supported by positive findings for the studies of the SAB and ABSSSI indications.
L782: ## 6.3.2. Clinical Success in Ukrainian Versus Non-Ukrainian Sites in Trial BPR-CS-009
L783: ## Issue
L784: In Trial BPR-CS-009, it was observed that sites in Ukraine showed substantially higher overall success rates compared to sites in other countries. Due to large site-specific efficacy and fewer AEs, these sites were identified for inspection but could not be inspected due to the current travel restrictions to Ukraine. Thus, in addition to clinical site inspections, an Applicant inspection was also conducted (see Section 10 for details), and higher overall success in Ukraine was evaluated in further detail.
L785: ## Background
L786: There may be limitations with generalizing Trial findings across different geographical regions. Overall response rates in non-Ukrainian countries may be lower than rates observed in the Trial BPR-CS-009, which included Ukrainian sites with high response rates. Ukraine was also the highest-enrolling country in the Trial, with 46.5% of subjects (180/387) in the mITT population. This may also have implications for the assumptions used in justifying the non-inferiority margin since the subject populations of Ukraine may not be appropriate for inclusion due to inherently lower risk factors and more effective therapeutic interventions compared to those of the assumed study population.
L787: Based on post-hoc analyses, subjects enrolled in Ukraine were younger and had a more favorable distribution of Baseline categories for complicated SAB, e.g., the percentage of subjects on chronic dialysis was 0.6% (1/180) in Ukraine compared to 23.2% (48/207) in other countries, and there were no subjects with LIE from Ukraine vs 4.8% (10/207) in other countries. Therapeutic interventions with the potential for achieving source control for SAB were performed more often within 72 hours before, or within 7 days after, randomization, in subjects from Ukraine than in other countries, e.g., in 70.5% for abdominal abscesses in Ukraine compared to 9.1% in abdominal abscesses in other countries, and in 67.9% (74/109) in ABSSSIs/soft tissue infections in Ukraine compared to 30.5% (30/128) in other countries. (Table 45).
L788: ## **Assessment**
L789: Significantly higher overall success rates based on DRC at the PTE visit were observed in Ukraine (86.7%, 156/180 across treatment arms) versus other countries excluding Ukraine (54.1%, 112/207 across treatment arm). The rate difference (Ukraine – non-Ukraine) was highly significant at 86.7% versus 54.1%, difference favoring Ukraine by 32.6% (95% CI: 23.9, 40.8), p&lt;0.0001.
L790: As shown in Table 45, treatment comparisons of overall success rates based on DRC assessment at PTE were 74/88 (84.1%) vs. 82/92 (89.1%) in Ukraine versus 58/101 (57.4%) versus 54/106 (50.9%) in other countries (excluding Ukraine). Since comparisons in Ukraine were less favorable for the ceftobiprole arm, the inclusion of Ukrainian sites likely did not positively influence the overall finding of non-inferiority.
L791: ## **Conclusion**
L792: As noted above, concerns were lessened since the between-arm difference was not more favorable in Ukraine versus the other countries. However, real life comparisons of rates may be lower than what was observed in this Trial due to the high rates observed in Ukraine, therefore comparisons of rates in the potential labeling should describe the strong differences in overall success rates between Ukrainian and non-Ukrainian sites.

L802: ## 7. Safety (Risk and Risk Management)
L803: ## 7.1. Potential Risks or Safety Concerns Based on Nonclinical Data
L804: The nonclinical safety profile of ceftobiprole medocaril sodium has been explored in single and repeat-dose studies in mice, rats, dogs, rabbits and monkeys for up to 3 months duration; in vitro and in vivo genotoxicity studies; reproductive and developmental toxicity studies including fertility studies in male and female rats, embryofetal developmental studies in rats and monkeys, and pre- and post-natal developmental toxicity study in rats; and PK and toxicokinetic studies to support ceftobiprole medocaril sodium development and to compare PK in animals and humans. The target organs of toxicity that may be relevant to human risks are described below.
L805: ## Injection Site Reactions, Thrombi, Emboli, Convulsions, Mortality
L806: Thrombi formation at the injection site was a consistent finding in toxicological studies across species, including rats, marmosets and dogs with severity increasing with dosing duration. In 2-4- and 13-week studies in rats, marmosets, and dogs, injection site findings included thrombus formation, accumulation of inflammatory cells, thickening of the vascular wall in the periphery of the dosing catheter, granulomas, edema/hemorrhage and/or necrosis of tissues around the catheter. No other significant toxicities were observed in 2-week studies in rats and in 4-week studies in rats and marmosets administered ceftobiprole medocaril sodium (at doses up to 360 mg/kg/day (1.4-times the maximum recommended human dose [MRHD] based on body surface area [BSA] comparisons) and 200 mg/kg/day respectively, (0.75 times the MRHD, based on BSA comparisons). However, in the 13-week studies in the rats and marmosets at similar doses to those used in shorter term studies, convulsions and mortality were observed (\ge 50 mg/kg in marmosets, 0.2 times the MRHD; \ge 250 mg/kg in rats, 0.94 times the MRHD, based on BSA comparisons). Thrombi/emboli were seen in marmosets in several tissues distal to the site of injection, including in skeletal muscle, heart, and lungs, that were attributed to the cause of mortality at all doses tested. In the rat 13-week study, mortality was primarily attributed to kidney failure (see kidney toxicity information below). Although no seizures or thrombi (except at the injection site) were reported in the dog 13-week study (up to 32 mg/kg/day, 0.4 timed the MRHD, based on BSA comparisons), the dosing catheter in many animals did not remain patent for the duration of the study and was found to be filled with fibrin, erythrocyte clumps and inflammatory cell infiltrate. In mice, tonic/clonic convulsions were observed after ceftobiprole medocaril sodium was administered as a single intravenous dose at \ge 250 mg/kg (0.75 times the MRHD, based on BSA comparisons).
L807: ## Kidney Toxicity
L808: No significant kidney toxicities were observed in 2- or 4-week studies in rats or in 4-week studies in marmosets. However, in a 13-week rat study at doses up to 750 mg/kg/day in males (2.8 times the MRHD, based on BSA comparisons) and 376 mg/kg/day in females (1.42 time the MRHD, based on BSA comparisons), significant kidney toxicity (dose dependent increases in tubular/duct eosinophilic bodies, and presence of foreign material) was observed at \ge 250 mg/kg/day potentially due to precipitation of test article; kidney interstitial fibrosis (moderate) was observed in males at the high dose. Mortality was observed at \ge 250 mg/kg/day,
L809: primarily on study Days 34 to 87 and attributed to kidney failure due to obstruction with foreign material. Mice administered a single dose of ceftobiprole medocaril sodium intravenously at \ge 250 mg/kg showed kidney tubules deposits (moderate to marked), dilation, congestion, degeneration of distal tubules and necrosis. In this study the lethal dose in mice was \ge 500 mg/kg (0.94 the MRHD based on BSA comparisons).
L810: ## **Hypersensitivity**
L811: In a 2-week dog study, ceftobiprole medocaril sodium administered intravenously at \ge 50 mg/kg/day (0.6 times the MRHD based on BSA comparisons) induced a histaminergic reaction (reddening of the skin, face edema, injection of the oral mucosa, vomiting and salivation) primarily associated with a relatively short infusion time (30 minutes). Findings significantly decreased with a longer infusion time (2 hours) for the high and medium dosed animals. These findings correlated with a dose dependent increase in plasma levels of histamine that returned to control levels after approximately 4 hours from start of infusion. In a 13-week dog study, ceftobiprole medocaril sodium administered intravenously at up to 32 mg/kg/day (0.4 times the MRHD based on BSA comparisons) caused sporadic reddening of the gums of some dogs primarily during the first 3 weeks of dosing. Ceftobiprole medocaril sodium administered to guinea pigs by the intravenous or subcutaneous route, at a dose up to 100 mg/kg (0.5 times the MRHD based on BSA comparisons), showed moderate antigenic potential.
L812: ## 7.2. Potential Risks or Safety Concerns Based on Drug Class or Other Drug-Specific Factors
L813: Ceftobiprole is a cephalosporin antibacterial drug. In general, cephalosporins have a favorable safety profile and have been well-tolerated with extensive use worldwide. Common adverse reactions associated with their use include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and rash. Labeled Warnings and Precautions across the five generations of cephalosporins include serious hypersensitivity/anaphylactic reactions, *Clostridioides difficile* associated diarrhea, neurotoxicity including seizures and encephalopathy, development of drug-resistant bacteria with prolonged or inappropriate use, and laboratory-based abnormalities such as direct Coombs' test seroconversion and decrease in prothrombin activity. Almost all cephalosporins require dose adjustment in subjects with impaired renal function. The second generation cephalosporins carry a risk of hearing loss in pediatric subjects while third generation cephalosporins such as ceftriaxone may interact with calcium containing products, or cause pancreatitis, biliary sludge, gallbladder pseudolithiasis, and hemolytic anemia. Third and fourth generation cephalosporins have rarely been associated with electrolyte derangements including hyponatremia and hyperkalemia.
L814: Reported post-marketing adverse events for cephalosporins include serum sickness-like reaction, acute tubulointerstitial nephritis, and acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis. A few cases of neonatal death in subjects receiving ceftriaxone in conjunction with calcium-containing fluids have been reported. Hepatotoxicity or drug induced liver injury due to cephalosporins are uncommon with the exception of ceftriaxone which as noted above can cause biliary sludge related to the formation of ceftriaxone-calcium salt. Finally, there have been reports of life-threatening or fatal occurrences of encephalopathy, myoclonus and seizures related to cefepime use. This was primarily observed in subjects with renal impairment who exceeded recommended dosages but have also occurred in subjects in whom doses were appropriately adjusted.
L815: Given its drug class, the risks and safety concerns for ceftobiprole are anticipated to be similar to those associated with cephalosporins already on the market as summarized above. Adverse events of special interest monitored by the Applicant during the clinical development program of ceftobiprole included hypersensitivity/anaphylactic reaction, *C. difficile* colitis, convulsions, acute renal failure, increased hepatic enzymes, hyponatremia, nausea, vomiting, and thrombosis.
L816: ## 7.3. Potential Risks or Safety Concerns Identified Through Postmarket Experience
L817: A review of the literature regarding the postmarketing experience for ceftobiprole yielded a retrospective case series conducted in Italy reporting on 29 patients who received ceftobiprole; 2 patients developed myoclonus and 1 patient developed a rash that were attributed to ceftobiprole (Durante-Mangoni et al. 2020). No deaths occurred in patients while receiving ceftobiprole. Another published case reported agranulocytosis in a patient receiving ceftobiprole after DRESS associated with vancomycin and rifampin (Wendland et al. 2011). After discontinuation of ceftobiprole, the patient's neutrophils recovered without further issues. The Applicant has also submitted postmarketing surveillance data in their application highlighting cases of serious hypersensitivity reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, urticaria, and angioedema.
L818: The FDA Adverse Event Reporting System was also queried for AEs reported with ceftobiprole. Upon review, AEs that were deemed potentially related to ceftobiprole were leukopenia, encephalopathy, rash, agranulocytosis, hyponatremia, and seizures.
L819: Review of the labeling from Canada, the United Kingdom, and Australia did not identify any new safety issues. Safety issues and adverse reactions reported in the ex-US labeling were derived from the clinical studies covered in this review. No additional postmarketing experiences were identified.
L820: ## 7.4. FDA Approach to the Safety Review
L821: Please see the discussion in Section 3.2 for a description of the clinical trials and any other data used in the review of safety and whether the trials submitted were fit for purpose. The studies submitted for safety were analyzed individually as described in this section. Pooling of safety results was not deemed to be appropriate given clinically distinct subject populations and differences in study design and conduct across pivotal trials. No major data quality or integrity issues were identified that would preclude performing a safety review for this NDA. There were no major identified issues with respect to recording, coding and categorizing AEs. A few preferred terms (PTs) were reclassified based on the verbatim terms. The clinical data scientist performed standard safety analyses including Food and Drug Administration Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities queries (FMQs) to determine safety signals, and additional analyses as requested by the clinical team. The clinical review team performed a grouped query (GQ) analysis for selected treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) to evaluate potential splitting of similar AEs and these are discussed in the TEAE section of each indication. Review of subject narratives and graphical subject profiles (created using JMP clinical version 17) were used in some instances to help determine causality. AE and TEAE are used interchangeably in this review.
L822: ## NDA 218275
## Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
L823: Safety evaluations included recording of AEs, vital signs (including electrocardiogram results), and collection of laboratory parameters. For all studies, AEs included any untoward medical occurred associated with the use of the drug in humans, whether or not considered drug related. An AE could arise with any use of the drug (e.g., off-label use, use in combination with another drug) and with any route of administration, formulation, or dose, including an overdose. If there was a suspicion that a GQ was related to ceftobiprole, subject narratives and graphical subject profiles (created using JMP clinical version 17) were used to help determine causality.
L824: For Trial BPR-CS-009, AEs were collected continuously from the start of first dosing up to and including the scheduled PTE visit (Day 70 \pm 5 days post-randomization). For Trial BPR-CS-008, AEs were collected continuously from start of first dosing up to and including the scheduled last follow-up visit (28-35 days after last treatment). The Medical Dictionary for Regulatory activities (MedDRA) version 24.0 was used for both Trials. In order to assess severity, a 3-point grading scale was used (mild, moderate, severe). For Trial CAP-3001, AEs were collected from the time of informed consent up to completion of the last trial-related procedure. For BAP 248307, AEs were collected from the first study related procedure up to the last trial-related procedure. MedDRA version 10.0 was used for studies CAP-3001 and BAP 248307. For Trial BPR-PIP-002, AEs were collected continuously from time of first study drug administration up to and including the scheduled last follow-up visit (28-35 days after EOT). MedDRA version 22.1 was used for this Trial.
L825: ## 7.5. Adequacy of the Clinical Safety Database
L826: The Applicant conducted eighteen phase 1 studies in adults and two phase 1 studies in pediatric subjects for a total of 464 subjects. The studies enrolled 385 adult subjects and 79 pediatric subjects who received ceftobiprole. The ceftobiprole dose ranged from 125 mg to 1000 mg. Additional information on the phase 1 safety database can be found in Section 17.
L827: The duration of exposure in each of the studies submitted for safety evaluation are noted in the table below. A total of 1315 subjects were treated with ceftobiprole in these studies. The dosing, duration, and number of subjects in the safety database of all submitted phase 3 studies were considered sufficient to conduct a safety review.

L832: ## 7.6. Safety Results
L833: ## 7.6.1. SAB, Trial BPR-CS-009
L834: ## 7.6.1.1. Overview of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events Summary, Trial BPR-CS-009
L835: As shown in Table 47 the overall incidence of TEAEs was 63.4% in the ceftobiprole arm and 59.1% in the daptomycin arm. Most of the TEAEs in the ceftobiprole arm were of moderate severity and there were slightly fewer severe TEAEs as compared to the daptomycin arm. There was an overall lower incidence of SAEs in the ceftobiprole arm compared to the daptomycin arm, respectively (18.8% versus 22.7%). The number of deaths and TEAEs leading to discontinuation were similar between treatment arms.
L836: There were four subjects in the ceftobiprole arm and none in the comparator arm with TEAEs leading to dose modification of the study drug. In the ceftobiprole arm, two subjects each required dose reduction and dose interruption, described below:
L837: - Subject (b) (6) had a reported TEAE of acute kidney injury resulting in reduction of the ceftobiprole dose on Day 6. However, on the same day, the subject also developed SAEs of respiratory failure and staphylococcal pneumonia which led to the permanent discontinuation of ceftobiprole.
- Subject (b) (6) had a reported SAE of renal impairment on Day 6 resulting in ceftobiprole dose reduction. The dose was reduced for 2 days until the creatinine improved. Ultimately, the subject died from cardiopulmonary failure.
- Subject (b) (6) had a reported TEAE of allergic dermatitis on Day 16 which led to ceftobiprole dose interruption and treatment for the rash on the same day. Ceftobiprole was permanently discontinued on Day 18 after a positive dechallenge and rechallenge associated with fevers and an elevated eosinophil count 8.5% (reference range 0-6). The subject recovered and no other signs of hypersensitivity were reported.
- Subject (b) (6) had a reported TEAE of dyspnea resulting in ceftobiprole dose interruption on Day 4 which was considered possibly related by the investigator. However, dyspnea resolved upon continuation of ceftobiprole.

L847: ## 7.6.1.2. Deaths, Trial BPR-CS-009
L848: There were no imbalances in TEAEs leading to death between the treatment arms (17/191 (8.9%) in the ceftobiprole and 18/198 (9.1%) in the daptomycin arm). In both arms, the most commonly reported TEAE leading to death was multiple organ dysfunction syndrome and septic shock.
L849: None of the TEAEs leading to death were assessed as drug related by the investigator or by the FDA reviewer upon a detailed review of the case narratives. The case narratives and subject profiles suggested that the deaths appeared to be related to underlying comorbidities and complications arising from the underlying infection, which is not unexpected for subjects with SAB. A meta-analysis performed in 2022 estimated that the all-cause mortality rate of SAB in a total of 341 studies (536,791 subjects, spanning from January 1, 1991 to May 7, 2021) was 10.4% (95% CI, 9.0%–12.1%) at 7 days, 13.3% (95% CI, 11.1%–15.8%) at 2 weeks, 18.1% (95% CI, 16.3%–20.0%) at 1 month, 27.0% (95% CI, 21.5%–33.3%) at 3 months, and 30.2% (95% CI, 22.4%–39.3%) at 1 year (Bai et al. 2022).
L850: The mortality rate in the BPR-CS-009 trial of 8.9% at Day 70 was less than what was seen in the meta-analysis by Bai et al. described above, possibly due to mortality being assessed in a clinical trial setting.

L865: In addition, the incidence of deaths was examined in the subgroup of subjects with endocarditis (n = 15 in ceftobiprole arm, n = 10 in daptomycin arm) as these subjects would be expected to have greater severity of illness and underlying comorbidities. Overall, there were no major imbalances in death among subjects with endocarditis. In subjects with RIE, there was one death (b) (6) in the ceftobiprole arm (6.7%) compared to none in the daptomycin arm. The TEAE leading to death in the ceftobiprole arm was cardiopulmonary failure, attributed to underlying cardiopulmonary comorbidities (history of cardiac failure and multiple cardiac valvular abnormalities).
L866: ## 7.6.1.3. Serious Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events, Trial BPR-CS-009
L867: The incidence of SAEs was lower in the ceftobiprole arm compared to the daptomycin arm (18.8% versus 22.7%). Most SAEs occurring in both arms were related to the Infections and Infestations system organ class (SOC) (9.4% in the ceftobiprole versus 12.6% in the daptomycin arm). Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome was the only SAE that had a greater than 1% risk difference in the ceftobiprole arm versus the daptomycin arm. After reviewing the narratives of the subjects who experienced an SAE of multiple organ dysfunction syndrome while on ceftobiprole (b) (6), none of these SAEs appeared to be drug-related, or due to failure of treatment with ceftobiprole.
L868: Additional SAEs were evaluated to determine relatedness to ceftobiprole, and selected SAEs are described below by SOC. The FDA reviewer agreed with the investigator that two SAEs (seizure and leukopenia) could have been related to ceftobiprole. There were two additional SAEs (tonic-clonic seizure and cutaneous vasculitis) may also have been related to ceftobiprole, and the FDA reviewer's causality assessment for these selected SAEs is noted below:
L869: ## Blood and Lymphatic System Disorders
L870: - Subject (b) (6) had an SAE of leukopenia on Day 14. On that day, his WBC decreased to 3.02 \times 10^3/\mu\text{L} (9.95 \times 10^3/\mu\text{L}) with an absolute neutrophil count of 1.76 \times 10^3/\mu\text{L}. On Day 18, ceftobiprole was discontinued due to leukopenia. The subject was switched to vancomycin and the next recorded neutrophil count occurred on Day 21 where the absolute neutrophil count was 1.52 \times 10^3/\mu\text{L}. He was lost to follow-up, and it was unknown if the WBC recovered. Concomitant medications included metamizole, potassium supplements, bromhexine, and tramadol. The FDA reviewer agrees with the investigator that this SAE was possibly related to ceftobiprole.
L871: ## Infections and Infestations
L872: - Subjects (b) (6) in the ceftobiprole arm had SAEs of pneumonia (2 fatal). There did not appear to be a relationship between these SAEs and ceftobiprole as pneumonia was likely acquired nosocomially due to complicated medical histories and prolonged hospitalization prior to starting ceftobiprole. Both SAEs occurred on Day 2 of ceftobiprole treatment in two subjects who had organisms isolated other than *S. aureus*: (b) (6) had pneumonia due to *Acinetobacter bereziniae*, with an MIC of 0.12 to ceftobiprole; (b) (6) had *K. pneumoniae* bacteremia likely to pre-existing mediastinitis, complicated by pericarditis, pneumonia, and multiple organ dysfunction). The other subject (b) (6) developed pneumonia on Day 16, 12 days after leaving against medical advice. All three subjects were considered treatment failures.
L873: ## Nervous System Disorders
L874: As described below, two subjects in the ceftobiprole arm, who had no past medical history of seizures, developed SAEs of seizures that were temporally associated with ceftobiprole. Cephalosporins can precipitate seizures and seizures are noted as warnings in the labeling of several drugs in this class (Bora et al. 2016). The FDA reviewer agrees with the inclusion of seizures and other central nervous system disorders in the warnings section of labeling as proposed by the Applicant.
L875: - Subject [REDACTED](b)(6) had no medical history of seizure and developed an SAE of a generalized tonic-clonic seizure on Day 15 while on ceftobiprole, in the setting of worsening renal function, and other TEAEs including nausea, vomiting, hypotension, multiple organ failure with respiratory distress requiring endotracheal intubation. While there may have been confounding factors such as hypotension and possible hypoxia due to respiratory distress requiring intubation, an association to ceftobiprole cannot be completely excluded.
- Subject [REDACTED](b)(6) had a medical history of alcohol abuse but no history of seizures and developed an SAE of seizure on Day 11 during infusion of ceftobiprole which led to discontinuation. At the time of the seizure, the subject was still conscious but was unresponsive to a verbal challenge with a fixed glare. There were no concomitant medications or events at the time that would predispose to seizures, and there was no renal impairment. The FDA reviewer agrees with the investigator that this SAE was probably related to ceftobiprole.
L876: ## Renal and Urinary Disorders
L877: - Subject [REDACTED](b)(6) had an SAE of acute kidney injury on Day 24, two days after completion of treatment with ceftobiprole. The baseline creatinine was 1.02 mg/dL (Day -1) and increased to 1.3 mg/dL on Day 14 and 2.92 mg/dL on Day 21. On Day 34, a biopsy of the kidney was performed which showed acute glomerulonephritis with IgA deposits associated with *S. aureus* infection. Due to the biopsy results, it is unlikely that there was a direct relationship between acute kidney injury and ceftobiprole. On Day 66, the subject died due to respiratory failure.
- Subject [REDACTED](b)(6) had an SAE of renal impairment on Day 6 (see 7.6.1.4). It is unlikely that the renal impairment was primarily caused by ceftobiprole as the creatinine decreased while on ceftobiprole, and there were other confounding factors (i.e., infection, diuretic usage, cardiac issues).
L878: ## Skin and Subcutaneous Disorders
L879: - Subject [REDACTED](b)(6) had an SAE of cutaneous vasculitis on Day 27, 6 days after the last dose of ceftobiprole. It was characterized by petechiae on the subject's hands for which a biopsy was performed and showed leukocytoclastic vasculitis with transepidermal ischemic necrosis. After topical treatment, the SAE resolved. Ceftobiprole may have been associated with this SAE as other beta-lactams have been shown to cause leukocytoclastic vasculitis (Baigrie 2024). However, cutaneous vasculitis can also be idiopathic or associated with infections.
