L892: ## 7.6.1.4. Adverse Events and FDA Medical Queries Leading to Treatment Discontinuation, Trial BPR-CS-009
L893: In both arms, the number of subjects who had AEs leading to treatment discontinuation was comparable (9.4% in the ceftobiprole arm and 9.1% in the daptomycin arm). The most common types of TEAEs that led to treatment discontinuation were related to the Infections and Infestations SOC.
L894: The AEs considered possibly related to the study drug by the investigator and leading to treatment discontinuation in the ceftobiprole arm were leukopenia (n = 1), gastrointestinal
L895: ## NDA 218275
## Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
L896: disorders (n = 3), seizure (n = 1), allergic dermatitis (n = 2), urticaria (n = 2), and liver enzyme elevation (n = 1). These subjects are described below:
L897: - Subject [REDACTED](b)(6) had AEs of nausea, vomiting, gamma-glutamyl transferase increased (93 U/L on Day 1 to 528 U/L on Day 10), blood alkaline phosphatase increased (166 U/L on Day 1 to 708 U/L on Day 10), ALT increased (19 U/L on Day 1 to 229 U/L on Day 10), AST increased (21 on Day 1 to 165 U/L on Day 10) on Day 8 resulting in treatment discontinuation on Day 9. Nausea resolved by Day 15 and liver enzymes were within normal limits by Day 35.
- Subject [REDACTED](b)(6) had an AE of urticaria on Day 15 which was characterized by itching and a rash on the thorax, abdomen, and extremities. Symptoms improved initially with desloratadine, but the subject reported intensified itching and worsening rash which required intravenous methylprednisolone. On Day 16, the urticaria intensified again and ceftobiprole was discontinued.
- Subject [REDACTED](b)(6) had an AE of urticaria on Day 18 which was also characterized by a rash that disappeared spontaneously but reappeared at a different site the following day. Because of the continuous symptoms, ceftobiprole was discontinued.
- Subject [REDACTED](b)(6) had an AE of allergic dermatitis (verbatim term was a macular-papular skin rash) on Day 9 which continued the following day. The subject was treated with chloropyramine and ceftobiprole was discontinued with resolution of the subject's rash by Day 13.
- Subject [REDACTED](b)(6) had an AE of allergic dermatitis on Day 16. The subject had a reported fever of 38.4°C along with a raspberry-colored shallow rash. Ceftobiprole was temporarily interrupted (i.e., 1 dose was skipped) and the subject was treated with prednisolone and chloropyramine leading to disappearance of the rash. On Day 18, after infusion of ceftobiprole, the rash and fever recurred, leading to permanent discontinuation.
- Subject [REDACTED](b)(6) had an SAE of seizure on Day 11 leading to discontinuation of ceftobiprole. Subject was discussed in the SAE section.
- Subject [REDACTED](b)(6) had an SAE of leukopenia on Day 14 leading to discontinuation of ceftobiprole. Subject was discussed in the SAE Section (7.6.1.3).
L898: The FDA reviewer agrees with the Applicant about the possible causality between the above AEs (leukopenia, gastrointestinal disorders, seizure, allergic dermatitis, urticaria and liver enzyme elevation) and ceftobiprole. In addition, the most common adverse reactions leading to discontinuation (nausea, vomiting, rash, and urticaria) will be proposed in Section 6 in labeling.

L907: ## 7.6.1.5. Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events, Trial BPR-CS-009
L908: TEAEs occurred in 63.4% of the subjects in the ceftobiprole arm and 59.1% in the daptomycin arm with a risk difference of 4.3%. The GQs demonstrating a risk difference of at least 4% or higher in the ceftobiprole arm compared to the daptomycin arm were nausea, vomiting, hypokalemia, pneumonia, and diarrhea; these are described below. Hypokalemia is discussed in the laboratory Section 7.6.1.6. Although the GQ of bacterial infections were common in both arms, it was not considered an adverse reaction as they were likely related to underlying medical conditions and was not caused by ceftobiprole.
L909: NDA 218275
Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
L910: ## **Gastrointestinal Symptoms**
L911: Most TEAEs of either nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea were of mild to moderate severity and did not lead to discontinuation. About half of the TEAEs of nausea or vomiting were related to ceftobiprole by the investigator.
L912: There were no reports of diarrhea associated with *Clostridioides difficile*. Gastrointestinal symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea are often considered common adverse reactions associated with antibacterial drugs, and are proposed by the Applicant in Section 6 of labeling.
L913: ## **Pneumonia**
L914: The narrow FMQ of pneumonia encompassed the PTs of pneumonia, pneumonia staphylococcal, pneumonia aspiration, lung abscess, pneumonia pseudomonal, pneumonia viral, and infectious pleural effusion. Although the number of subjects with pneumonia was higher in the ceftobiprole arm compared to the daptomycin arm [16 (8.4%) versus 5 (2.5%)], review of subject profiles and narratives did not reveal a link between ceftobiprole and the PTs in the narrow FMQ. Out of the 16 subjects with FMQs of pneumonia, 2 were due to aspiration and 1 was due to a viral cause. In most of the cases the subjects had comorbidities which made pneumonia more likely to occur (presence of endotracheal tube, immunosuppression, prolonged hospitalization). There was also no information about the pathogen except in 4 cases, where all but one of the pathogens isolated was gram negative. The subject with a *S. aureus* pneumonia is described below:
L915: - One subject, [REDACTED](b) (6), had an AE of pneumonia staphylococcal on Day 7. The subject was on cefazolin for 6 days for persistent SAB prior to randomization. After 6 days of ceftobiprole, the subject experienced an SAE of respiratory failure and MSSA was isolated from lavage from the endotracheal tube; ceftobiprole was discontinued and changed to imipenem-cilastatin. The AEs of pneumonia staphylococcal and respiratory failure were resolved 2 days later. Overall, given that the AE occurred even after 6 days of cefazolin and 6 days of ceftobiprole but resolved after 2 days of imipenem-cilastatin suggests either a source control issue or an issue related to incomplete duration of treatment. This subject was considered a treatment failure due to use of non-study antibacterial drugs.
L916: Analysis of the following adverse events of special interest were performed as these AEs have been observed with use of other cephalosporins or noted in the nonclinical studies using ceftobiprole: renal impairment, leukopenia, liver enzyme increased, thrombosis, rash, hypersensitivity reactions, and seizure. Leukopenia and liver enzyme increased are discussed in the laboratory section. Thrombosis will be discussed in Section 7.7.2, key safety review issues.
L917: ## **Renal Impairment**
L918: There were 13 subjects (6.8%) who experienced AEs related to the GQ of renal impairment (renal impairment, blood creatinine increased, creatinine renal clearance decreased, acute kidney injury, and oliguria) in the ceftobiprole arm, and there was a similar frequency in the daptomycin arm. Although none appeared to have a definitive association between renal impairment and ceftobiprole, there was a possible association in 2 subjects ([REDACTED](b) (6)). Blood creatinine increased was proposed by the Applicant in labeling, and a few additional PTs noted in this section will be added.
L919: - Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) is an 82-year-old male with a medical history of cellulitis and creatinine renal clearance decrease. As he finished his 28-day course of ceftobiprole, his
L920: ## NDA 218275
## Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
L921: creatinine slowly increased and on the final day of ceftobiprole, the creatinine was measured at 1.81 mg/dL (1.37 mg/dL on Day 1). Concomitant medications which could have also caused the increase in creatinine included metamizole and omeprazole. Overall, the contribution of ceftobiprole cannot be completely excluded. However, there were confounding factors such as history of renal impairment, advanced age, and concomitant medications.
L922: - Subject (b) (6) is a 66-year-old male with a medical history of diabetes mellitus and hypertension. Levels of creatinine started to increase from Day 14 from 1.07 mg/dL to 1.49 mg/dL on Day 28, the day that ceftobiprole treatment was completed. Concomitant medications included omeprazole, furosemide, and ketoprofen. On Day 29, his creatinine improved to 1.1 mg/dL. Although there were confounding factors such as concomitant medications and underlying comorbidities which could have caused the increase in creatinine, the contribution of ceftobiprole cannot be completely excluded.
L923: ## **Rash/ Hypersensitivity**
L924: There were 3 (1.6%) subjects each in the ceftobiprole arm with the AEs of rash (b) (6) and hypersensitivity (b) (6) compared to 2 (1%) subjects in the daptomycin arm with the AE of rash and 1 (0.5%) subject in the daptomycin arm with the AE of hypersensitivity.
L925: In the subjects with AEs of rash, 2 of the 3 subjects (b) (6) were considered by both the Applicant and the MO to have been related to ceftobiprole. These cases are discussed in AEs leading to discontinuation.
L926: In subjects with AEs related to hypersensitivity, the MO considered that all three AEs could have been related to ceftobiprole. Subjects (b) (6) experienced the AE of urticaria are discussed in the AEs leading to discontinuation section and subject (b) (6) experienced the AE of cutaneous vasculitis and is discussed in the SAE section.
L927: ## **Seizure**
L928: There were 3 (1.6%) subjects in the ceftobiprole arm with AEs related to seizure (b) (6). Subjects (b) (6) discussed in the SAE section, had seizures that may have been associated with ceftobiprole. However, for subject (b) (6) the seizure was clearly attributed to hypoglycemia as multiple episodes of hypoglycemia (nadir of 23.4 mg/dL) were reported. None of the subjects had a past medical history of seizures.

L972: ## 7.6.1.6. Laboratory Findings, Trial BPR-CS-009
L973: ## Chemistry
L974: Chemistry findings between the two arms were similar with exception of decreased potassium, elevated chloride, elevated random glucose, elevated albumin and elevated blood urea nitrogen (BUN) which had more than a 2% risk difference of occurring in the ceftobiprole arm than in the daptomycin arm. None of the differences in the chemistry findings, with exception to hypokalemia, were felt to be directly due to ceftobiprole given that chemistry derangements are
L975: ## NDA 218275
## Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
L976: common in critically ill subjects. There were no laboratory measurements for lipase, amylase, phosphate, magnesium, calcium, and bicarbonate.
L977: ## Hypokalemia
L978: There was a greater frequency of AEs of blood potassium increased (GQ of hypokalemia) in the ceftobiprole arm as compared with the daptomycin arm, as shown in Table 52 above; this correlated with an increased number of subjects in the ceftobiprole arm with low potassium values as noted in the table below. Hypokalemia could be explained by increased gastrointestinal losses caused by diarrhea and vomiting; both of which were higher in the ceftobiprole arm. As such, hypokalemia will be added to the Applicant's proposed labeling as an adverse reaction.
L979: Moreover, in the ceftobiprole arm, there were 14 subjects with a low potassium value of level 3. In contrast, 9 subjects in the daptomycin arm had the same level with a risk difference of 2.8%, higher in the ceftobiprole arm. Subject profiles were evaluated for cardiac events that could be associated with hypokalemia. Upon examination of the 14 subjects, two subjects had AEs related to cardiac arrhythmias, atrial fibrillation and arrhythmia, described below:
L980: - Subject (b) (6) reported an AE of arrhythmia on Day 12. The subject had a medical history of hypertension, myocardial ischemia, myocardial infarction, diabetes mellitus, renal failure, cardiac ventricular thrombosis, decubitus ulcer, intermittent hypokalemia, intermittent hypernatremia, and atrial fibrillation. The nadir for potassium measurement occurred on Day 3 where it was measured at 2.3 mmol/L and the subject was given potassium chloride. On Day 12, the subject experienced an SAE of arrhythmia and despite cardiopulmonary resuscitation and adrenaline, the subject died. No potassium level was recorded on this day with the last potassium level of 3.2 mmol/L being recorded on Day 7.
- Subject (b) (6) reported an AE of atrial fibrillation on Day 5. The subject had a medical history of atrial fibrillation, venous thrombosis, and aortic valve sclerosis. The lowest potassium measurement occurred on Day 21 where it was measured at 2.8 mmol/L. The subject did not receive any potassium supplementation for hypokalemia but was on a standing order of electrolyte replacement (calcium chloride, magnesium chloride, potassium chloride and sodium chloride).

L1001: ## **Hematology**
L1002: There were 6 subjects (3.2%) in the ceftobiprole arm who had a low neutrophil count of level 3 (&lt;0.5 \times 10^3/\mu\text{L}) (b) (6) compared to the daptomycin arm which had 3 subjects (1.5%). When assessing the timing and concomitant medications, it appeared that in 4 of these 6 cases, the neutropenia could have been associated with ceftobiprole (b) (6). In most cases, the AEs related to low WBC counts occurred later in the course of ceftobiprole (after Day 20). Of note, leukopenia has been proposed by the Applicant in section 6 of labeling.
L1003: - Subject (b) (6) was a 70-year-old female with a medical history of iron deficiency anaemia and hypertension who had a neutrophil count of 9 \times 10^9/\text{L} on Day 1. Her neutrophil count slowly declined until the end of her ceftobiprole therapy when it was 0.6 \times 10^9/\text{L} on Day 36. There was a reported AE of leukopenia on Day 35. She was not receiving any concomitant medications but was given filgrastim on Day 35. Her neutrophil count recovered back to Baseline on Day 42.
L1004: Three of these instances of ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection (b) (6) did not have any corresponding AEs related to low neutrophil counts (b) (6)
L1005: (e.g., neutropenia, leukopenia, lymphopenia, or white blood cell decreased), and these subjects are described below:
L1006: - Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) was a 63-year-old female with a medical history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and anemia who had a neutrophil count of 10.3 \times 10^9 /L on Day 1. Her neutrophil count gradually decreased to 0.09 \times 10^9 /L on Day 28 when she finished her course of ceftobiprole. Her neutrophil count recovered to 6.86 \times 10^9 /L on Day 42. Because there were no concomitant medications and the neutrophil count improved after discontinuation of ceftobiprole, there is a possibility that ceftobiprole caused the neutropenia.
- Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) was a 64-year-old female with a medical history of diabetes mellitus type 2 who had a neutrophil count of 9.1 \times 10^9 /L on Day 1. The subject finished a 27-day course of ceftobiprole and on Day 28, the neutrophil count was 0.03 \times 10^9 /L. On Day 35, the neutrophil count recovered to 4.03 \times 10^9 /L. Besides ceftobiprole, the subject was also on omeprazole from Day -2 to Day 18. However, because the neutrophil continued to decrease even after omeprazole was discontinued, it appeared to be more likely that ceftobiprole caused the neutropenia.
- Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) was a 47-year-old male with a medical history of chronic kidney disease requiring hemodialysis, myocardial infarction, chronic cardiac failure, and anaemia. The subject had a neutrophil count of 12.49 \times 10^9 /L on Day 1. On Day 22, his neutrophil count was 0.49 \times 10^9 /L. The subject also experienced cardiac failure on this day and died on the next day. Concomitant medications that were administered for more than 10 days included dexketoprofen from Day -2 to Day 23 and esomeprazole from Day 5 to Day 23. Although there are other confounding factors, it was possible that the neutropenia could have been related to ceftobiprole.
L1007: Subject profiles with AEs related to neutropenia were also reviewed. Of these, 3 subjects [REDACTED](b) (6) were not included in Table 55 below, laboratory values exceeding specified levels (i.e., with neutrophils &lt; 0.5 \times 10^3/\mu L):
L1008: - Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) was a 55-year-old male with a medical history of chronic hepatitis C, anaemia, chronic cardiac failure, and drug dependence found to have endocarditis and septic pulmonary embolism. On Day 3, the neutrophil count was 1.75 \times 10^9 /L (6.78 \times 10^9 /L on Day 1) and continued to stay at this level until ceftobiprole was stopped on Day 21 when the neutrophil count was 1.53 \times 10^9 /L. On Day 22, after ceftobiprole was discontinued, the investigator reported an AE of neutropenia as the neutrophil count had decreased to 0.37 \times 10^9 /L. There were no recorded labs after this day. Although the subject was not on any prolonged concomitant medications known to cause neutropenia, due to the quick onset and that there was no further decrease of the neutrophils while on ceftobiprole, it is unlikely that the neutropenia was associated with ceftobiprole, although it is not fully excluded.
- Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) was an 89-year-old female with a medical history of anaemia, and decreased creatinine renal clearance. On Day 7, the subject had a neutrophil count of 1.04 \times 10^9 /L (12.5 \times 10^9 /L on Day 1) while still on ceftobiprole therapy. The subject finished ceftobiprole therapy on Day 13. As there were no further measurements of neutrophil counts after Day 7, it could not be determined if there was a temporal association with ceftobiprole.
- Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) who developed an SAE of leukopenia and associated decreased in absolute neutrophil count is discussed in Section 7.6.1.3.
L1009: ## NDA 218275
## Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
L1010: Subject profiles with a low lymphocyte level 3 (i.e., &lt;0.5 \times 10^3 cell/\muL) were examined as well as subjects with AEs of either lymphocyte count decreased or lymphopenia (b) (6). No subjects had profiles suggesting ceftobiprole as the cause of isolated low lymphocyte counts.
L1011: Subject profiles with a low hemoglobin level 3 (i.e., decreased by &gt;2 g/dL from Baseline) were examined for any possible signals of drug-induced hemolytic anemia which has been seen with other cephalosporins or other causes of drug related anaemia such as bone marrow suppression. No subjects had any significant patterns in hemoglobin values or laboratory abnormalities (increased lactate dehydrogenase, low haptoglobin, increased bilirubin) to suggest drug-induced hemolytic anemia; or chronology to suggest bone marrow suppression. In 11 of these subjects, the level 3 decrease in hemoglobin occurred after ceftobiprole was discontinued while 14 occurred within 7 days of starting ceftobiprole. Four subjects required transfusions. For most of the subjects, the hemoglobin initially decreased but increased while on ceftobiprole treatment without the need for transfusions. Overall, no subjects exhibited a decrease in hemoglobin to suggest ceftobiprole as a cause. Furthermore, when comparing subjects who experienced the AE of anaemia in the ceftobiprole arm compared to the daptomycin arm, both arms experienced the same number of AEs (13.1%). By the PTE, both arms had similar mean change from Baseline.

L1022: ## 7.6.1.7. Assessment of Drug-Induced Liver Injury, Trial BPR-CS-009
L1023: Overall, the number of subjects in the four screening quadrants for drug-induced liver injury (DILI) were generally balanced between the two treatment arms. There were no identified cases of Hy's law in the ceftobiprole treatment arm.
L1024: One subject (b)(6) in the ceftobiprole arm, represented by a blue dot in Figure 7, was in the potential Hy's Law quadrant but did not meet the criteria for Hy's Law as he did not have an alkaline phosphatase level of less than 2x the upper limit of normal. Also, prior to being randomized to ceftobiprole, the subject already had elevated liver enzymes (AST &gt;3x upper limit of normal [ULN] and total bilirubin &gt;5x ULN).
L1025: Graphical profiles of subjects noted in the cholestasis and temple's corollary quadrants were reviewed and elevated liver tests did not appear to be solely attributed to ceftobiprole.

L1033: There were a few outliers with one or more liver test abnormality, as noted in Table 57 below. One subject had elevation in transaminases of &gt; 10x ULN and one had an elevation in bilirubin &gt;3 x ULN which are detailed below.
L1034: - Subject (b) (6) had a medical history significant for hypertension, chronic cardiac failure, chronic pancreatitis, stage 5 chronic kidney disease with an AV fistula, who developed ALT and AST \ge10x ULN. On Day 14, peak values of 755 U/L (baseline of 5 U/L) for ALT, 960 U/L for AST (baseline of 11U/L), 170 U/L for alkaline phosphatase (baseline of 59 U/L), and 64 U/L for gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) (baseline of 13 U/L). On Day 21, all liver related lab values decreased while on ceftobiprole (AST was 50 U/L and ALT 238 U/L). If the elevations were caused by ceftobiprole, it would be expected that there would be continued elevation or worsening of the liver enzymes. According to the investigator and FDA Reviewer, the transaminase elevation was less likely due to ceftobiprole. However, since there were no other apparent causes of the laboratory abnormalities, such as concomitant medications or other infection besides the primary infection, drug-induced transaminitis could not be fully excluded.
- Subject (b) (6) had a &gt;3x ULN elevation in bilirubin on Day 8 (from 166 U/L on Day 1 to a peak of 708 U/L on Day 10). There were also increases in AST (20.5 U/L on Day 1 to 164.8 U/L on Day 10), ALT (19 U/L on Day 1 to 229.4 U/L on Day 10) and GGT (93 U/L on Day 1 to 528 U/L on Day 10). Ceftobiprole was discontinued on Day 9 and all values started to decrease on Day 13 and normalized by Day 41. The FDA reviewer agrees with the investigator that it is probable that ceftobiprole could have caused elevations of the liver enzymes given the temporal association.

L1070: ## **7.6.1.9. Subgroup Analyses, Trial BPR-CS-009**
L1071: Several subgroups were examined based on demographic variables. For most subgroups, the percent of AEs occurred at similar rates. However, there was a higher percentage of AEs in subjects ≥65 years old in the ceftobiprole arm as compared to the daptomycin arm. There was also a higher percentage of AEs seen in subjects ≥65 years old compared to subjects ≤65 years old within the group of subjects receiving ceftobiprole, however, the types of AEs seen were similar. A similar trend was seen among subjects ≥75 years old, however, the size of this subgroup was small. In the subgroup of subjects ≥75 years old, there was a similar frequency of SAEs (seven subjects in the ceftobiprole arm (41%) experienced 13 SAEs while 10 subjects in the daptomycin arm (48%) experienced 19 SAEs). In terms of mortality, there were 6 deaths in the ceftobiprole arm (35%) compared to 7 deaths in the daptomycin arm (33%). The FDA reviewer agrees with the investigator that none of these SAEs or deaths in the ceftobiprole arm could be attributed to the drug.
L1072: In addition, the majority of subjects were White, non-Hispanic or Latino, and from outside of the US. The frequency of AEs in these subgroups was similar to the frequency of AEs occurring in the entire safety population. The other demographic groups were too small to make any conclusions regarding safety, but no major differences are anticipated.

L1078: ## 7.6.2. Acute Bacterial Skin/Soft Tissue Infection, Trial BPR-CS-008
L1079: ## 7.6.2.1. Overview of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events Summary, Trial BPR-CS-008
L1080: The overall incidence of TEAEs was 44.3% in the ceftobiprole arm and 38.3% in the vancomycin and aztreonam arm. Most TEAEs in the ceftobiprole arm were mild or moderate, and there were fewer severe TEAEs as compared to the vancomycin and aztreonam arm (2.7% versus 7.0%). There was a lower incidence of SAEs in the ceftobiprole versus the vancomycin and aztreonam arm (1.8% and 3.5%, respectively). Treatment discontinuation due to TEAEs was also lower in the ceftobiprole arm compared to the vancomycin and aztreonam arm (1.8% versus 2.9%).
L1081: Five subjects in each arm had interruptions of their respective treatment. In the ceftobiprole arm, the AEs leading to interruption were blood creatinine increased in two subjects and the following in one subject each: pruritus, vomiting, and both headache and nausea. None were SAEs and all subjects recovered.

L1102: ## NDA 218275
## Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
L1103: The following subjects in the ceftobiprole arm had SAEs. SAEs related to AEs of special interest such as pneumonia and thromboembolism are also discussed in this section. Of the six SAEs, rash and pruritis were probably related to ceftobiprole.
L1104: - Subject (b) (6) had a reported an SAE of rash and pruritis causing prolonged hospitalization. This was a 49-year-old male with no significant past medical history who developed an erythematous papular pruritic rash over his trunk and extremities 10 days after starting ceftobiprole for which ceftobiprole was discontinued. Concomitant medications included paracetamol, omeprazole, and enoxaparin. Two days after discontinuing ceftobiprole and receiving methylprednisolone and antihistamine therapy, the rash was completely resolved without sequelae. Due to the lack of other concomitant medications that have a high likelihood of causing the SAEs along with the temporal relationship, the FDA reviewer agrees with the investigator that the SAE was probably related to ceftobiprole.
- Subject (b) (6) had a reported an SAE of bronchial obstruction causing prolonged hospitalization. This was an 82-year-old female with a medical history of arterial hypertension who developed bronchospasms, cough, tachypnea, and scarce expectoration after 3 days of ceftobiprole treatment. She finished a 5-day regimen and ultimately, she recovered from the broncho-obstructive syndrome. The FDA reviewer agrees with the Applicant that the SAE was not related to ceftobiprole because despite the continuation of ceftobiprole, the broncho-obstructive symptom did not worsen.
- Subject (b) (6) had a reported an SAE of pneumonia causing hospitalization. This was a 64-year-old male with a medical history significant for alcohol use, methamphetamine abuse, IV heroin use, who was hospitalized for acute CAP approximately one month after ceftobiprole was discontinued (end of ceftobiprole treatment was Day 11 and hospitalization on Day 37). The FDA reviewer agrees with the investigator that the SAE was not related to ceftobiprole.
- Subject (b) (6) had a reported SAE of skin bacterial infection causing hospitalization. She was a 34-year-old female with a medical history of intravenous heroin use, tobacco use, and schizo-affective schizophrenia who, after 5 days of ceftobiprole, had worsening of primary ABSSSI with tenderness, warmth, erythema, and pain. A CT scan showed a well-defined area of fluid collection anterior to the deep fascia of the right thigh, slightly extending to the lateral aspect suggesting abscess formation. Incision and drainage were not done because the subject left before the procedure took place. While she was inpatient, she received two days of piperacillin-tazobactam, 1 day of meropenem, and 1 day of levofloxacin. By Day 35, the worsening of primary ABSSSI was considered resolved. The FDA reviewer agrees with the investigator that the SAE was not related to ceftobiprole as this could have been related to incomplete source control or worsening infection due to risk factors associated with intravenous drug use.
L1105: - Subject (b) (6) had a reported SAE of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) causing hospitalization. This was a 39-year-old male with a medical history of intravenous heroin drug use, tobacco use, past tibial/fibula fractures who was randomized to ceftobiprole for right calf cellulitis. On the day of randomization, the subject complained of bilateral lower leg swelling with moderate pain and redness with the latter two symptoms starting 10 days prior. A DVT was found on ultrasound and the subject was admitted to the hospital 5 days after starting ceftobiprole; ceftobiprole was discontinued and switched to non-study antibacterial drugs. Because the subject had symptoms of a DVT prior to starting ceftobiprole, the FDA reviewer agrees with the investigator that the SAE is unlikely related to ceftobiprole.
L1106: ## 7.6.2.4. Adverse Events and FDA Medical Queries Leading to Treatment Discontinuation, Trial BPR-CS-008
L1107: The incidence of AEs that led to treatment discontinuation was lower in the ceftobiprole arm compared to the vancomycin and aztreonam arm (1.8% versus 2.9%). The AEs that led to treatment discontinuation in the ceftobiprole arm included rash, pruritus, dysgeusia, deep vein thrombosis, wound infection, and skin bacterial infection. The subjects with AEs of rash, pruritis, and deep vein thrombosis leading to discontinuation are discussed in the Section 7.6.2.3.
L1108: The only AE that led to more than one discontinuation was skin bacterial infection (one is discussed in the SAE section, and one is noted below):
L1109: - Subject (b) (6) was a 36-year-old female with a medical history of intravenous heroin use, diabetes mellitus type II, and hepatitis C who, after 6 days of ceftobiprole, continued to have worsening of primary ABSSSI (started on Day 3). Ceftobiprole was discontinued on Day 6 and the AE resolved on Day 35. No other concomitant antibacterial drugs were given during Day 0 and Day 35 (when the subject was discontinued from the trial). The worsening of primary ABSSSI could be interpreted as the lack of efficacy of ceftobiprole in this subject rather than an AE per se; however, given that no additional antibacterial drugs were initiated, it is difficult to comment on the association of this event with ceftobiprole. The investigator considered it unrelated to trial drug.

L1116: ## 7.6.2.5. Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events, Trial BPR-CS-008
L1117: AEs occurred in 148 of 334 subjects (44.3%) in the ceftobiprole arm and in 131 of 342 subjects (38.3%) in the comparator arm. The AEs that occurred with a risk difference of \ge 1\% in the ceftobiprole arm were gastrointestinal-related such as nausea (10.8% vs 5.6%), diarrhea (6.3% vs 4.7%), and dysgeusia (2.1% vs 0%). All AEs of nausea, vomiting or diarrhea were of mild to moderate severity and the majority had dose interruption or modification. More than half of these AEs were thought to be possibly/probably related to ceftobiprole by the investigator. As with the 009 trial, the GQ of bacterial infection was common in both arm but was not related to ceftobiprole and likely related to underlying medical conditions and was therefore, not included in the label.
L1118: There were no reports of diarrhea associated with *Clostridioides difficile*. Gastrointestinal symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea are often considered common adverse reactions associated with antibacterial drugs, and are proposed by the Applicant in labeling.
L1119: ## Leukopenia
L1120: The AEs related to leukopenia were reported in three subjects in the ceftobiprole arm (0.9%) and 2 subjects in the vancomycin and aztreonam arm (0.6%). The TEAEs in the ceftobiprole arm

L1123: ## **Renal Impairment**
L1124: There were 2 subjects in the ceftobiprole arm (0.6%) and 4 subjects in the vancomycin and aztreonam arm (1.2%) who experienced AEs related to the GQ of renal impairment (blood creatinine increased occurred in 2 subjects receiving ceftobiprole and acute kidney injury occurred in 4 subjects receiving vancomycin and aztreonam). The 2 subjects who experienced the AE of blood creatinine increased both had the decreasing creatinine while on ceftobiprole therapy, making it unlikely that ceftobiprole caused the AE.

L1162: While there was a higher incidence of level 2 decrease in creatinine clearance in the ceftobiprole arm (2.2% vs 0.6%), level 2 creatinine elevations were lower in the ceftobiprole arm (0.9% vs. vs 2.4%). Both arms had similar mean changes in creatinine from baseline throughout the trial and returned to Baseline by the last follow-up.

L1170: ## NDA 218275
## Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
L1171: While there were no subjects in the ceftobiprole arm with a low WBC of level 3, there were 5 subjects in the ceftobiprole arm with a low lymphocyte count of level 3. All subjects, except for one subject (b) (6), had low lymphocyte counts prior to being randomized to ceftobiprole and this subject is discussed below:
L1172: - Subject (b) (6) was a 54-year-old male with a medical history of drug abuse and tobacco use and a lymphocyte count of 1.5 \times 10^9/L on Day -1 who had an AE of lymphopenia with a lymphocyte count of 0.3 \times 10^9/L on Day 5. The patient finished the course of treatment on Day 6 and the lymphocyte count normalized by Day 16. The only concomitant medication was lidocaine, which would not be expected to cause lymphopenia. Overall, it is unclear if ceftobiprole could have caused the lymphopenia as the decrease could have been related to the primary infection.
L1173: There was one subject in the ceftobiprole arm with a low neutrophil count of level 3:
L1174: - Subject (b) (6) is a 34-year-old male with a medical history of tobacco abuse, alcohol use, drug abuse, and seizure who had a neutrophil count of 10.9 \times 10^9/L on Day -1. On Day 5, the neutrophil count decreased to 0.1 \times 10^9/L and on Day 6, the subject finished his course of ceftobiprole, and neutrophil count increased to 5.2 \times 10^9/L on Day 7. There was no reported AE of neutropenia. The decrease in neutrophils was unlikely to be related to ceftobiprole given the short course of the drug and likely decreased due to resolving infection.
L1175: In addition, there were subjects with AEs related to hematological abnormalities. There were 2 subjects (b) (6) with AEs of neutropenia and 1 subject (b) (6) with an AE of lymphopenia in the ceftobiprole arm.
L1176: Regarding subject (b) (6) the neutrophil count was 1 \times 10^9/L on Day 2 and increased while on ceftobiprole. For subject (b) (6) the onset of neutropenia was 12 days after ceftobiprole was discontinued. There is no information regarding medications taken or other AEs around the time of treatment discontinuation. In both cases, onset of neutropenia does not suggest a strong correlation with ceftobiprole. For subject (b) (6) the lymphocyte count decreased daily from 1.4 \times 10^9/L on Day 1 to a nadir of 0.3 \times 10^9/L on Day 5. Ceftobiprole was discontinued on Day 6 and the lymphocyte count increased from the nadir on Day 7 and returned to baseline on Day 16 (next lab draw after Day 7). There were no other concomitant medications that could have caused this, but infection/sepsis could have contributed to the decrease.
L1177: Overall, the change in leukocytes from baseline through the last follow-up were similar between arms and decreased as expected as infection resolved.

L1188: ## 7.6.2.7. Assessment of Drug-Induced Liver Injury, Trial BPR-CS-008
L1189: The analysis of drug-induced liver injury identified PTs related to liver injury in eight (2.4%) subjects treated with ceftobiprole and eleven (3.2%) subjects treated with the comparator (vancomycin and aztreonam). There were no Hy's law cases detected.

L1196: ## **AEs relating to hepatic injury:**
L1197: The AEs reported in the ceftobiprole arm include gamma-glutamyl-transferase increased, alanine aminotransferase increased, aspartate aminotransferase increased, and blood alkaline phosphatase increased. None were categorized as severe TEAEs, SAEs, or TEAEs resulting in treatment discontinuation.
L1198: The investigator considered that ceftobiprole was a possible cause of the elevated liver enzymes in four subjects ( [REDACTED] (b)(6) ) in the ceftobiprole arm. The cases are described below:
L1199: - Subject [REDACTED] (b)(6) is a 59-year-old male with a medical history of hepatitis C, and drug abuse who had reported AEs of AST and ALT increased on Day 5, which was the last day of ceftobiprole treatment. There were no concomitant medications and therefore it could have been possible that ceftobiprole caused the elevated liver enzymes. However, elevated liver enzymes secondary to infection cannot be ruled out.
L1200: ## NDA 218275
## Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
L1201: In the other three cases involving increase in liver enzymes, alternative reasons for liver enzyme elevation were more likely or the timing of the AE was not well correlated with ceftobiprole treatment. These are noted below:
L1202: - Subject [REDACTED](b) (6), a 29-year-old female with a medical history of alcohol use and drug abuse, reported an AE of AST and ALT increased on Day 32. The subject received ceftobiprole only on Day 1 and liver enzymes obtained on Day 3 were within normal limits (ALT 19 U/L, AST 23 U/L). The limited exposure to ceftobiprole and the timing of the AE did not appear to correlate well with exposure to ceftobiprole.
- Subject [REDACTED](b) (6), a 31-year-old male with a medical history of drug abuse and alcohol use, began having elevated ALT and AST on Day 3. While still on ceftobiprole, the subject's AST decreased from 141 U/L on Day 3 to 87 U/L on Day 5. Furthermore, after stopping ceftobiprole on Day 5, the AST increased to 108 U/L on Day 16. Because of the inconsistent LFT changes, the reviewer found it unlikely that ceftobiprole caused the elevated liver enzymes, although it cannot be completely excluded.
- Subject [REDACTED](b) (6), a 40-year-old male with a medical history of hepatitis C and drug abuse, had an elevated AST of 208 U/L on Day 3 (from 68 U/L on Day 1). The AST decreased to 192 U/L while still on ceftobiprole and continued to decrease once discontinued. Furthermore, the bilirubin was 13.68 µmol/L on Day -1 and decreased while on ceftobiprole to 8 µmol/L on Day 5. Because of this, it was unlikely that ceftobiprole caused the elevated liver enzymes.

L1213: ## 7.6.2.8. Vital Signs' Analyses, Trial BPR-CS-008
L1214: ## Heart Rate, Temperature, Respiratory Rate
L1215: The mean changes from Baseline to post-treatment in both arms were similar and within normal ranges.

L1218: ## 7.6.2.9. Subgroup Analyses, Trial BPR-CS-008
L1219: Table 72 shows the incidence of common TEAEs by demographic subgroups of sex, age, ethnicity, and race. The incidence of TEAEs in the ceftobiprole arm was higher in subjects between the age of 18 to 34 years and the most common TEAEs are discussed below. There were more TEAES in the subgroup of subjects ages 65-75 years in the ceftobiprole arm as compared to the vancomycin and aztreonam arm, but the number of subjects was too small to draw any meaningful conclusions. The majority of subjects were White, non-Hispanic or Latino, and from the US; the incidence of TEAEs appeared to be overall similar to the safety population. In addition, there did not appear to be imbalances in TEAEs by gender.
L1220: ## Age 18 to 34 years
L1221: In this age group, there was a higher percentage of subjects in the ceftobiprole arm (58.6%) who experienced AEs compared to the percentage of subjects in the vancomycin and aztreonam arm (40.3%). In addition, the percentage of TEAEs in the younger subgroup was higher than in the older subgroups receiving ceftobiprole. The most commonly reported AEs in the ceftobiprole arm were nausea (n = 14), headache (n = 5), diarrhea (n = 5), alanine aminotransferase increased (5 subjects), and aspartate aminotransferase increased (5 subjects). The most commonly reported AEs in the comparator arm were headache (6 subjects), diarrhea (5 subjects), nausea (4 subjects), abscess limb (4 subjects), and pyrexia (3). It appears that nausea and increased liver tests may have driven this difference between treatment arms in this subgroup of younger subjects. In this subgroup, there was one SAE each in the ceftobiprole arm (worsening of skin infection, (b) (6)) and vancomycin and aztreonam arm (cellulitis). There were no deaths in this subgroup.
L1222: ## Age 65-74 years
L1223: In this age group, there was a higher percentage of subjects in the ceftobiprole arm (48.1%) who experienced AEs compared to the percentage of subjects in the vancomycin and aztreonam arm (33.3%). The most commonly reported AEs in the ceftobiprole arm were blood creatinine increased (2 subjects), headache (2 subjects) and injection site reaction (2 subjects) while the most commonly reported AEs in the vancomycin and aztreonam arm were skin bacterial infection (3 subjects), nasopharyngitis (2 subjects) and oedema peripheral (2 subjects). There were 2 SAEs in the vancomycin and aztreonam arm (skin bacterial infection) and none in the ceftobiprole arm. There were no deaths in either treatment arm in this subgroup.

L1230: ## 7.6.3.1. Overview of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events Summary, Trial CAP-3001
L1231: **Table 73** shows the overview of adverse events in Trial CAP-3001. SAEs were balanced between the two treatment arms. The ceftobiprole arm also had more subjects with AEs overall at 70% compared to 64.6% in the ceftriaxone arm. This difference was driven mostly by more moderate AEs seen in the ceftobiprole arm. Severe and mild AEs were balanced between the two arms.

L1239: ## 7.6.3.2. Deaths, Trial CAP-3001
L1240: The deaths between the ceftobiprole arm and the ceftriaxone arm were balanced with 9 deaths in each treatment arm (Table 74). There was one subject in the ceftobiprole arm and two subjects in the ceftriaxone arm that had more than one AE leading to death. The majority of AEs leading to death were different between the two arms. For the ceftobiprole arm, lung neoplasms and cardiac failure were more common whereas in the ceftriaxone arm, pneumonia and sudden death were most common. Cardiac and respiratory AEs were common AEs leading to death in the two treatment arms which is consistent with the hospitalized Trial population.
L1241: Review of the narratives of subjects who had died confirmed the investigator assessment that none of the deaths in the ceftobiprole treatment arm were related to the study treatment. For the ceftriaxone treatment arm, the investigator attributed subject (b) (6)'s death to be likely related to the treatment. Review of the narrative confirms this assessment as the subject's pneumonia course continued to worsen requiring intensive care management likely due to ineffective treatment. The remaining deaths appear to be unrelated to study treatment.

L1249: ## 7.6.3.3. Serious Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events, Trial CAP-3001
L1250: SAEs were overall balanced between the two arms (Table 75). In addition, there was not an appreciable difference between the two arms with regards to the SOC of the SAEs. Within the ceftobiprole treatment arm, infections and infestations represented the highest group of SAEs (3.9%) followed by respiratory, thoracic, and mediastinal disorders (2.9%). One subject in the ceftobiprole arm developed anaphylactic shock. Subject (b) (6) had received 2 doses of ceftobiprole and during her third ceftobiprole dose, 1 hour into the infusion, the subject was found to be unconscious, pulseless, and apneic. Trial medication was discontinued, and the subject later fully recovered after resuscitation. Concomitant medications were not reported, and the investigator believed this event was related to the study drug. The labeling will include a warning for hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis.

L1261: ## 7.6.3.4. Adverse Events Leading to Treatment Discontinuation, Trial CAP-3001
L1262: The overall rate of AEs leading to discontinuation was low at less than 10% in each trial arm (Table 76). The ceftobiprole arm had a higher rate of AEs leading to discontinuation compared to ceftriaxone at 5.8% vs 3.7%. The higher rate of AEs leading to discontinuation in the ceftobiprole arm was mainly due to gastrointestinal disorders with subjects experiencing vomiting, abdominal pain, and nausea compared to 1 subject experiencing abdominal distension leading to discontinuation in the ceftriaxone arm. Similar to SAEs, infections and infestations disorders were also relatively common in both arms. These results suggest ceftobiprole is relatively well tolerated with the drug leading to discontinuation in a relatively small percentage of subjects. Of note, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain will be labeled as adverse reactions in Section 6 of labeling.

L1271: ## 7.6.3.5. Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events, Trial CAP-3001
L1272: There were slightly more TEAEs in the ceftobiprole arm (70%) compared to the ceftriaxone arm (64.6%; Table 77). However, there is a notable difference between the types of TEAEs in each treatment arm. The TEAEs that occurred at a greater frequency in the ceftobiprole arm compared to the ceftriaxone arm included nausea, vomiting, rash, phlebitis, and hemorrhage (\ge 2\% risk difference). Gastrointestinal related AEs were the most common AEs associated with the use of ceftobiprole. In addition, there are TEAEs in both arms that were balanced (liver enzyme
L1273: ## NDA 218275
## Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
L1274: increased, headache, abdominal pain, diarrhea, insomnia, dizziness), which may be due to both drugs being cephalosporins or due to underlying medical comorbidities. Pneumonia was also balanced in both arms occurring at a high frequency however this is likely due to the underlying illness of the subject. Please refer to Section 17.4 for the table of subjects with all AEs occurring in the safety population.
L1275: Given the higher frequency of hemorrhage in the ceftobiprole arm, these subjects were evaluated in greater detail. There were 4 cases of hemoptysis categorized under hemorrhage. Two of the subjects may have developed hemoptysis that did not have an obvious cause aside from their underlying pulmonary illness. Of the remaining two, one subject was on warfarin and aspirin and the other developed hemoptysis 12 days after receiving the last dose of ceftobiprole and was also diagnosed with lung cancer. For the other subjects who developed hemorrhage as an AE, three of the subjects were on anti-coagulant medications and 4 subjects developed their AE several days to weeks after receiving their last dose of ceftobiprole. There were two subjects that developed hematoma and ecchymoses without a clear inciting event, however one of the subjects had only received one day of treatment. Based on these evaluations, there does not appear to be a strong signal that would indicate ceftobiprole is associated with hemorrhage as several of the AEs were likely due to concomitant use of anti-coagulant medications or occurred after treatment.

L1296: ## 7.6.3.6. Laboratory Findings, Trial CAP-3001
L1297: The number of subjects with either high or low chemistry analyte values were generally balanced between the two treatment arms (Table 78). There were slightly more abnormalities in the ceftriaxone arm with low sodium and elevated BUN. Elevated creatinine was also seen more frequently in the ceftriaxone arm at 4.1% compared to 1.1% in the ceftobiprole arm (Table 79). There were more cases of high potassium (6.5% vs 3.6%) and low glucose (5.5% vs 3%) in the ceftobiprole subjects. Of note, hyperkalemia and hypoglycemia were reported as AEs less commonly for ceftobiprole compared to ceftriaxone. The number of subjects with liver abnormalities were balanced with no major differences between the two arms (Table 80). Total cholesterol and triglycerides were also balanced between the two arms (Table 81). Regarding hematology laboratory values, leukocytosis was observed more in the ceftriaxone arm at 31% compared with 24% in the ceftobiprole arm (Table 82). The remainder of abnormal hematologic values were otherwise balanced.
L1298: Overall, there does not appear to be any major difference between ceftobiprole and ceftriaxone with respect to chemical, renal, cholesterol, hepatic, or hematologic laboratory values.

L1340: ## 7.6.3.7. Assessment of Drug-Induced Liver Injury, Trial CAP-3001
L1341: Figure 11 shows a screening assessment for potential cases of DILI. Overall, the number of subjects in the four quadrants were generally balanced between the two arms (Table 83). There were two subjects in each treatment arm – subjects [REDACTED](b) (6) in the ceftobiprole arm and subjects [REDACTED](b) (6) in the ceftriaxone arm – that fit the criteria for potential Hy's Law.
L1342: - In the ceftriaxone arm, subject [REDACTED](b) (6) was found to have elevated ALT at 45 U/L, AST at 114 U/L, and bilirubin at 2.22 mg/dL prior to receiving study medication for 3 days. Alkaline phosphatase and GGT were also elevated. Repeat blood work on the third day showed normalized ALT but increased alkaline phosphatase, AST at 127 U/L, and bilirubin at 2.81 mg/dL with a decrease in GGT. Repeat blood work to assess resolution of elevated liver function tests was not done. The subject had elevated values prior to receiving the study drug which may be due to initial illness and during treatment there was both improvement and worsening of lab values. In this subject, it is unclear if the study treatment is related to the liver dysfunction, but it is unlikely given the overall trend.
- Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) did not have liver function tests prior to receiving ceftriaxone. After receiving treatment for 9 days, liver function tests were obtained and the subject had normal levels of ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, and GGT. Bilirubin was elevated at 4.39 mg/dL. Study drug was stopped on day 11 and on day 13, subject had elevated ALT at 575 U/L, AST at 1072 U/L, and increased bilirubin levels that peaked at 6.02 mg/dL. GGT and alkaline phosphatase remained normal throughout the study. Lab work done at the end of the study showed resolution of all liver function tests except a persistent mildly increased bilirubin. Subject had developed a rib fracture on day 10 and cardiac failure on day 34. Subject had also received ranitidine concurrently with study treatment. While rare, ranitidine has been associated with liver injury with resolution upon stopping medication and it is possible that concurrent use of ranitidine and other medications may have caused the hepatic injury.
L1343: ## NDA 218275
## Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
L1344: - In the ceftobiprole arm, subject (b)(6) was found to have elevated AST at 3861 U/L, ALT at 883 U/L, bilirubin at 2.81 mg/dL, and elevated GGT prior to receiving treatment for 4 days. While on treatment, ALT decreased while the alkaline phosphatase and GGT increased along with bilirubin which peaked at 5.79 mg/dL. AST was not done at the time. Repeat lab work done at the end of the trial showed resolution of elevated laboratory values except for GGT but that value of GGT had decreased to less than the initial elevated value. Given the elevated values prior to receiving the study drug with a subsequent decrease in some of the values while on treatment, it is less likely that the liver injury is due to the study drug. It is likely that the initial abnormal laboratory values were due to the initial illness.
- Subject (b)(6) had mildly elevated ALT, AST, and bilirubin prior to receiving ceftobiprole. Alkaline phosphatase and GGT were within normal range throughout the trial. Subject received 8 days of treatment and during treatment, ALT, AST, and bilirubin increased until the last day of treatment. ALT and AST levels peaked at 68 U/L and 105 U/L respectively. Repeat testing done days after stopping treatment showed decreasing ALT and AST however bilirubin continued to increase to a peak of 2.51 mg/dL. There was no repeat testing to trend resolution of the remaining elevated values. Approximately 47 days after last laboratory test, the subject was reported to have hepatic cirrhosis. Given the diagnosis of hepatic cirrhosis near the end of the trial, it is likely that the subject had underlying liver disease prior to enrollment. This is supported in the initial elevated lab values prior to starting treatment. Any association with ceftobiprole and DILI would be difficult to determine in this subject.
L1345: Based on these two subjects who met potential Hy's Law criteria, there is no signal associating ceftobiprole with DILI.

L1355: ## 7.6.3.8. Vital Signs' Analyses, Trial CAP-3001
L1356: Review of the vital signs data showed no clinical differences between the treatment arms. L1357: ## 7.6.3.9. Subgroup Analyses, Trial CAP-3001
L1358: Based on the sub-group analysis (Table 84), there were more subjects with reported AEs in the ceftobiprole arm reported in each sex, race, ethnicity, and geographic subgroup which is consistent with the higher rate of AEs in the general population. Of note, there were fewer ceftobiprole subjects with AEs in the older age groups (&gt;65 and &gt;75 years). Overall, there does not appear to be major differences in the incidence of AEs by subgroup beyond what was observed in the general trial population. Some of the differences in AEs between the two treatment arms may be due to low enrollment within that subgroup. For example, there were only 33 total subjects in the Black or African American subgroup.

L1367: The proportion of subjects with TEAEs was similar in the ceftobiprole arm and the comparator cephalosporin arm (31.9% vs. 29.5% respectively). There were seven SAEs in the ceftobiprole arm vs. two SAEs in the comparator arm during the study period which are discussed below in Section 7.6.4.3

L1384: The narratives for the SAEs that occurred in the ceftobiprole arm are provided below. Two of these SAEs - hypersensitivity and pneumonia - occurred during the IV treatment period and the remainder (pleuropneumonia, pneumonia (2 events), tonsillitis streptococcal, pharyngitis streptococcal, pleural effusion, and vomiting) occurred following transition to oral antibacterial drugs:
L1385: - Subject (b) (6) experienced two SAEs of hypersensitivity and pleural effusion. This 17-year-old female with no significant medical history was admitted for treatment of CABP. On Day 3 of ceftobiprole administration, during the infusion, she experienced facial and extremity edema, a diffuse itchy rash, high fever and sweating. There was no associated hypotension or bronchospasm. Ceftobiprole was discontinued and the subject was treated with IV dexamethasone and oral chloropyramine. Symptoms resolved in an hour, and she was transitioned to treatment with cefuroxime and levofloxacin. Two days later, a chest x-ray demonstrated bilateral pneumonia and right-sided pleural effusion and her antibacterial regimen was adjusted to cefuroxime and clindamycin. A follow-up chest x-ray 2 days later revealed progression of pneumonia at which time vancomycin was initiated. CT chest showed bilateral hydrothoraces which were categorized as an SAE due to prolongation of hospitalization. Bilateral chest tubes were placed. Amikacin and amoxicillin/clavulanate were started for persistent fever. She improved clinically, her chest tubes were removed and she was transitioned to oral levofloxacin. The FDA reviewer's evaluation supports the relatedness of the SAE of hypersensitivity to ceftobiprole because it occurred during the IV infusion. However, this reviewer agrees with the investigator that the SAE of pleural effusion is likely due to complications of pneumonia and unrelated to study drug.
- Subject (b) (6) was a 1-year-old male with no significant medical history who was hospitalized for CABP. He had an SAE of pneumonia on Day 1. He was noted to have tachypnea during initial screening for the trial. On the same day, the subject received the first dose of ceftobiprole but was transferred to the intensive care unit for worsening tachypnea and was placed on mechanical ventilation later that day. Due to persistent fever following the second dose of ceftobiprole, the study drug was discontinued, and the subject was started on ceftriaxone and clarithromycin. Because his therapy was switched prior to Day 4, this subject did not have a clinical response assigned on that day and was judged to have a category of "worsened" at EOT. His clinical outcome was failure at the TOC visit. This reviewer agrees with the investigator that the pneumonia is unlikely to be related to the study drug, given that symptoms were present prior to his receiving the first dose of ceftobiprole and subsequent clinical worsening occurred within 24 hours of the start of treatment. The narrative is
L1386: compatible with worsening of underlying infection and occurred too soon after ceftobiprole initiation to support relatedness to the drug.
L1387: - Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) was a 6-year-old female with a history of atrial septal defect and asthma, who had an SAE of pleuropneumonia. She was treated with ceftobiprole for CABP and appeared well at EOT. No information was provided regarding the anatomical location of the original CABP. Two weeks later, she developed fever and was diagnosed with an upper respiratory infection and subsequently with left-sided pleuropneumonia necessitating hospitalization. She was treated with ceftriaxone for a week with improvement. She was discharged home but returned again the following day - imaging showed left sided pneumonia with an effusion measuring 5.5 cm. She was hospitalized again and treated with ceftriaxone and azithromycin for another week. This subject had a clinical response of improved assigned at Day 4 and at EOT but was judged to have a clinical outcome of failure at the TOC visit. The occurrence of pleuropneumonia and a large effusion two weeks after initial treatment for CABP may be compatible with the development of a complicated pleural effusion or empyema; this reviewer agrees with the investigator that it is unlikely to be related to administration of ceftobiprole.
- Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) was a 2-year-old male who experienced an SAE of pneumonia. He was originally hospitalized for CABP and treated with ceftobiprole for 5 days, followed by 5 days of oral amoxicillin clavulanate. The location of his pneumonia was not specified. His clinical response at Day 4 was judged to be improved and cured at the EOT visit. Twelve days after the EOT visit, he developed low grade fever and was diagnosed with a new left lobar pneumonia for which he was hospitalized and transferred to the intensive care unit within two hours of admission due to worsening tachypnea, dyspnea and persistent fever. He was treated with ceftriaxone, meropenem, and clarithromycin during this hospitalization and improved with treatment. Because the new pneumonia was diagnosed 12 days after his first EOT visit, it could have represented failure of treatment of the initial pneumonia. His overall clinical outcome was judged by the investigator to be failure at the TOC visit. This reviewer agrees with the Applicant that it is likely not related to administration of the study drug.
- Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) was a 3-year-old female treated for CABP with ceftobiprole for 3 days followed by amoxicillin clavulanate for 7 days. Fourteen days after the TOC visit, she developed fever and cough and was diagnosed with the SAEs of streptococcal pharyngitis and tonsillitis streptococcal for which she was hospitalized and treated with amoxicillin-clavulanate. Because there was approximately 3 weeks between completion of ceftobiprole treatment for CABP and the onset of her tonsillopharyngitis, these SAEs were not judged to be related to ceftobiprole.
L1388: - Subject (b) (6) was a 2-year-old male who was treated for 4 days with ceftobiprole for CABP and then transitioned to oral cefuroxime for 7 days. He experienced 4 episodes of vomiting after the second dose of cefuroxime but vomiting resolved later that same day after treatment with IV glucose, granisetron, ranitidine, and normal saline. This was considered an SAE as it prolonged hospitalization for one day, but this reviewer agrees with the Applicant that the vomiting was unlikely to be related to ceftobiprole given that it was temporally related to administration of cefuroxime.
- Subject (b) (6) was a 4-year-old male with no significant medical history who was admitted with CABP and initiated on ceftobiprole. No details were provided regarding findings on initial imaging. He exhibited cough, persistent fever and hypoxemia continuing into Day 4 of study treatment and was diagnosed with pleuritis. Chest x-ray on Day 4 found a new blunted right costophrenic angle and chest ultrasound noted free fluid. The subject had a thoracostomy tube placed the same day with drainage of 250 mL of yellow fluid. Analysis of the pleural fluid showed polymorphonuclear leukocytes (&gt;25 per low-powered field) and 2+ gram-positive cocci on smear but was negative on culture. A chest tube was placed the following day, ceftobiprole was discontinued, and amikacin, meropenem, and vancomycin were started. Pleuritis was classified as an SAE as it resulted in prolongation of hospitalization. In this reviewer's opinion, the SAE is not a safety event per se, but rather appears to represent worsening infection which may have been the result of failure of treatment with ceftobiprole.

L1398: ## 7.6.4.5. Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events, Trial BPR-PIP-002
L1399: TEAEs occurred with similar frequency in both treatment arms – 31.9% of subjects in the ceftobiprole arm and 29.5% of subjects in the comparator cephalosporin arm (Table 88). The most common TEAEs in the ceftobiprole arm were vomiting (7.4% of subjects), viral infection (4.3%), headache (3.2%), pneumonia (3.2%), and alanine aminotransferase increased (3.2%), all with a risk difference of &gt;3.0 compared to the comparator arm while the most common AE in the comparator cephalosporin arm was diarrhea (9.1% of subjects, risk difference -7.0). The ceftobiprole arm had more AEs related to hypersensitivity, phlebitis, urticaria, and infusion site reactions (6 subjects compared to 1 in comparator cephalosporin arm). The ceftobiprole arm also had more AEs related to the lower respiratory tract including pleurisy, pleural effusion and pneumonia (3 subjects compared to 0 in comparator cephalosporin arm) which are likely reflective of the infection under study and the 2:1 enrollment in the ceftobiprole versus comparator arms.
L1400: There were only 5 subjects in the ceftobiprole arm with HABP included in the trial. Among these subjects, there were two AEs, chromaturia and pyrexia, neither of which were considered SAEs.

L1428: Hematology test values indicated similar trends in ceftobiprole and comparator cephalosporin arms respectively in WBC counts, both Level 1 elevated (63% versus 54.5% respectively were greater than 10,800 cells/mL) and Level 1 decreased (9.8% versus 9.1 % respectively were less than 3,500 cells/mL). However, 41.3% vs. 25% of subjects in the ceftobiprole vs. comparator arms respectively had Level 3 elevations in WBC counts. In keeping with the expected physiological response to infection, WBC measurements were in general, abnormal at the start of the trial and trended toward normal by the time of TOC visit. Clinically relevant Levels 2 and 3 neutropenia and thrombocytopenia were reasonably balanced between treatment arms. Other hematology analytes including hemoglobin, lymphocyte, and eosinophil counts all had similar changes in both treatment arms. Although pancytopenia is described in association with the cephalosporin class of medications, pneumonia, severity of illness as well as the duration of treatment may have contributed to changes in the hematology values seen in this trial.

L1437: ## 7.6.4.7. Assessment of Drug-Induced Liver Injury, Trial BPR-PIP-002
L1438: There were no Hy's Law cases. In the ceftobiprole arm, three subjects with CABP experienced transaminase elevation. One subject, [REDACTED](b) (6) had both ALT and AST elevation. The remaining two subjects, [REDACTED](b) (6) had ALT elevation alone.
L1439: - Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) was a 6-year-old male with no significant medical history who had elevation in both ALT and AST. Bilirubin remained normal throughout the trial. The subject's concomitant medications included antipyretics (paracetamol on Days 1-3 and ibuprofen) and IV fluids and he was transitioned to oral cefuroxime axetil on study Day 13. Discrepancies were noted in the ADBL dataset for this subject with varying ULN values for ALT and AST at different time points during the study period. Thus, the fold-elevation from ULN could not be accurately determined and instead, the maximum fold-elevation from baseline value is depicted for this subject in Table 92. Because the maximum values of AST and ALT occurred at EOT after a 13-day course of ceftobiprole, and there was minimal use of concomitant medications, relatedness to ceftobiprole is possible. However, the etiology of this subject's pneumonia was not determined and may have been contributory as well to the rise in liver enzymes.

L1470: ## 7.6.4.9. Subgroup Analyses, Trial BPR-PIP-002
L1471: **Table 96** shows the incidence of AEs by demographic subgroups of sex and age. The incidence of AEs in female subjects was higher in the ceftobiprole arm compared to the comparator cephalosporin arm (29.3% and 17.4% respectively). Information from Dr. Ines Pagan, the pharmacology/toxicology reviewer indicates that although there were no specific juveniles included in the animal studies for ceftobiprole, there were no significant differences in the toxicity profiles of females compared to males in these studies.
L1472: Fewer subjects in the 3 months to &lt;2 years and the 2 years to &lt;6 years age groups in the ceftobiprole arm had TEAEs (35.1% and 25% respectively) compared to the same age groups in the cephalosporin ± vancomycin arm (47.4% and 50% respectively). Conversely, more subjects in the 12 years to &lt;18 years age group in the ceftobiprole arm had TEAEs compared to the comparator arm (33% versus 0). However, the number of subjects in each of these categories was too small to draw any meaningful conclusions. There were no subgroup analyses performed for ethnicity or race given that all but one subject enrolled in the trial were White. This lack of ethnic diversity in the trial may limit generalizability of results to populations in the U.S.

L1476: ## 7.6.5. Hospital-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia and Ventilator-Associated Bacterial Pneumonia, Trial BAP 248/307
L1477: The BAP 248/307 Trial was submitted to augment the safety database of ceftobiprole. The Applicant is not seeking an indication for HABP/VABP. This trial will be briefly described below followed by a discussion of safety results.
L1478: BAP 248/307 was a phase 3, randomized, double-blind, active-control, prospective, multicenter trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of ceftobiprole compared to linezolid/ceftazidime in adult subjects diagnosed with HABP and VABP. Pertinent inclusion criteria included subjects clinically diagnosed with pneumonia after a minimum of 72 hours of hospitalization or residence in a chronic care facility and who had clinical signs/symptoms of pneumonia. Subjects who were pregnant or lactating, had renal impairment, hepatic dysfunction, who were HIV positive, or had a known or suspected condition that may have jeopardized adherence to protocol requirements were excluded from the trial. A total of 781 subjects were randomly assigned to the two study arms with a total of 772 subjects included in the safety analysis, 386 subjects in each arm. There were 567 subjects in the non-VABP subgroup (283 in the ceftobiprole arm and 284 in the linezolid/ceftazidime arm) and 205 subjects in the VABP subgroup (103 in the ceftobiprole arm and 102 in the linezolid/ceftazidime arm).
L1479: ## 7.6.5.1. Overview of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events Summary, Trial BAP 248/307
L1480: Table 97 summarizes the AEs in Trial BAP 248/307. SAEs occurred in slightly more subjects in the ceftobiprole arm at 36% compared to the linezolid/ceftazidime arm at 32%. More subjects developed AEs leading to discontinuation of study drug with 14% of the ceftobiprole subjects compared to 10% of the linezolid/ceftazidime subjects. There were also more subjects experiencing AEs leading to dose modification in the ceftobiprole arm. Overall AEs were balanced between the treatment arms at 78%. There were slightly more severe AEs in the ceftobiprole arm at 38% compared to 35% of the comparator arm.

L1487: ## 7.6.5.3. Serious Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events, Trial BAP 248/307
L1488: There were slightly more subjects with SAEs in the ceftobiprole arm compared to the linezolid/ceftazidime (Table 98). L1498: ## 7.6.5.4. Adverse Events Leading to Treatment Discontinuation, Trial BAP 248/307
L1499: The number of subjects with AEs leading to discontinuation is listed in Table 99. While the ceftobiprole arm had more subjects with AEs leading to discontinuation (14%) compared to linezolid/ceftazidime (10.4%), the difference was not driven by one particular SOC. The respiratory, thoracic, and mediastinal disorders SOC had the highest number of subjects with AEs leading to discontinuation in both treatment arms followed by infections and infestations and nervous system disorders. Upon review of the AEs listed, many of the AEs appear to be related to the underlying condition of the subjects. For example, pneumonia, sepsis, and acute respiratory distress syndrome are expected conditions in this subject population. Of note, hyponatremia was found to be associated with discontinuation of ceftobiprole in 4 subjects (1%) compared to 1 subject in the comparator arm (0.3%). Low sodium values are discussed in the “Laboratory Findings” subsection below.

L1507: ## 7.6.5.5. Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events, Trial BAP
## 248/307
L1508: TEAEs occurred in a similar proportion of subjects in the two treatment arms at 77.5% for ceftobiprole and 77.7% for linezolid/ceftazidime (Table 100). The TEAEs that had the highest incidence in the ceftobiprole arm were bacterial infection, diarrhea, respiratory failure, pyrexia, hypokalemia, hyponatremia, and vomiting. Of these TEAEs, vomiting, bacterial infection, pyrexia, and hyponatremia had a &gt;2% risk difference in the ceftobiprole arm compared to the linezolid/ceftazidime arm. There was also an imbalance in renal impairment and cardiac failure in the ceftobiprole arm compared to the linezolid/ceftazidime arm. The high incidence of overall TEAEs is likely due to the significant comorbidities of the subjects and their complicated disease course. A significant portion of subjects in this trial required intensive care management with extensive medical histories contributing to their illness. Of the TEAEs with an imbalance, bacterial infection and cardiac failure were likely related to underlying medical conditions. Hyponatremia was also noted in the laboratory findings (see section below). Vomiting was noted in the other clinical studies as associated with ceftobiprole. Renal impairment was not observed when examining the laboratory data (see Laboratory Findings section below). Please refer to Section 0 for the table of subjects with all AEs occurring in the safety population.

L1533: ## 7.6.5.6. Laboratory Findings, Trial BAP 248/307
L1534: The tables below summarize the laboratory data from Trial 248/307 (Table 101, Table 102, Table 103, Table 104, and Table 105). In the ceftobiprole treatment arm, there were more cases of hyponatremia (19.4%) compared to the linezolid/ceftazidime treatment arm (14%). It appears this difference in cases of hyponatremia was largely driven by mild cases (between 130 and 132 mEq/L). The remainder of the chemistry values were relatively balanced between the two treatment arms. Of note, hyponatremia will be listed as an adverse reaction in section 6 of labeling. Evidence of renal dysfunction in each arm was also overall balanced with elevated creatinine occurring in 8.4% of subjects in the ceftobiprole arm vs. 7.5% in the linezolid/ceftazidime arms. While in the ceftobiprole arm there were more cases of elevated alkaline phosphatase at 24.1% compared to linezolid/ceftazidime at 15.5%, elevations in AST, ALT, and bilirubin levels were overall balanced between the two arms and did not exceed more than 10% of all subjects. Elevations in cholesterol levels were also balanced between the two arms, however there were more cases of hypertriglyceridemia in the ceftobiprole arm (52.2%) compared to the linezolid/ceftazidime arm (43.3%). Outliers in hematology values were also overall balanced between the two arms, but lymphopenia occurred more in the ceftobiprole arm (33.1%) than linezolid/ceftazidime (27.7%).
L1535: Overall, there does not appear to be major differences in the laboratory values between the treatment arms. The subject population in the Trial was fairly ill with multiple medical comorbidities that may be contributing to certain laboratory value outliers.

L1572: ## 7.6.5.7. Assessment of Drug-Induced Liver Injury, Trial BAP
## 248/307
L1573: Figure 15 shows a screening assessment for potential cases of DILI. Overall, the number of subjects in the four quadrants were generally balanced between the two arms (Table 106). There were two subjects in the ceftobiprole arm – subjects [REDACTED](b) (6) – that fit the criteria for potential Hy's Law.
L1574: - Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) had normal levels of ALT, AST, and alkaline phosphatase and mildly elevated bilirubin and GGT prior to enrollment. The subject received 7 days of ceftobiprole, and lab work done on Day 7 showed increasing levels of all liver enzymes and bilirubin values with ALT and AST peaking at 784 U/L and 1612 U/L, respectively, and with a bilirubin at 8 mg/dL. The subject was also progressing to multi-organ system failure and expired on day 7. The subject's worsening trajectory of illness confounds the association between ceftobiprole and DILI as the elevated liver enzymes could also be attributed to the multi-organ system failure.
- Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) had elevated ALT at 49 U/L and bilirubin at 5.2 mg/dL prior to receiving treatment. On Day 4, repeat lab work was obtained which showed increasing ALT at 103 U/L, AST at 78 U/L, bilirubin at 8.71 mg/dL. Alkaline phosphatase and GGT were also elevated. Ceftobiprole was stopped at this time. Repeat blood work was done again on Day 8 which showed ALT, AST, and bilirubin down-trending while alkaline phosphatase and GGT were shown to be increased. No further blood work was performed. Upon enrollment, subject had also received multiple other antibacterial drugs including piperacillin-tazobactam and gentamicin for 1 day. Concurrent administration of these drugs may have contributed to an increase in all of the liver enzymes as piperacillin-tazobactam can cause elevated ALT, AST, and bilirubin.
L1575: ## NDA 218275
## Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
L1576: The association between DILI and ceftobiprole is unlikely based on the results of this trial. The severity of illness in the subjects with concurrent use of hepatotoxic medications likely caused the elevated liver enzymes.

L1589: ## 7.7. Key Safety Review Issues
L1590: ## 7.7.1. Higher Mortality for Ceftobiprole Patients With VABP in Trial BAP 248/307
L1591: ## Issue
L1592: Increased deaths were observed in the VABP subgroup of Trial BAP 248/307 in subjects in the ceftobiprole arm compared to the linezolid/ceftazidime arm.
L1593: ## **Background**
L1594: In Trial BAP 248/307, a subgroup analysis was done on the safety population based on their pneumonia diagnosis. Of the total 772 subjects, there were 205 VABP subjects with 103 subjects in the ceftobiprole arm and 102 in the linezolid/ceftazidime arm. It was noted that VABP subjects in the ceftobiprole arm had a higher rate of death compared to the subjects in the linezolid/ceftazidime arm. Although the trial was not submitted for an evaluation of efficacy, the increased deaths may have represented a safety issue in this subgroup of subjects. An in-depth analysis of the data was conducted to evaluate potential causes and reasons for the increased deaths in the VABP subgroup.
L1595: ## **Assessment**
L1596: The total deaths in Trial BAP 248/307 were overall balanced between both arms (23% ceftobiprole vs. 22% linezolid/ceftazidime). In the HABP (non-VABP) subgroup however, there were fewer deaths in the ceftobiprole arm at 18.7% compared to 21.1% in the linezolid/ceftazidime arm. This is contrasted by more deaths in the VABP subgroup among ceftobiprole subjects (33%) compared to the linezolid/ceftazidime arm (23.5%). Given this higher rate of death, the narratives for all the deaths in the BAP 248/307 trial were reviewed to determine whether the study drug was related to death. The study drug and death were considered unrelated by the FDA reviewer if the death occurred within 48 hours of receiving the first dose of treatment, the death occurred after receiving the last dose of treatment, or another cause of death was established in the narrative. If a subject who was diagnosed with VABP, initiated treatment, and subsequently expired within a day, the study drug likely would have not made a difference in the subject's trajectory and the death was deemed unrelated to the treatment. In addition, if a subject completed treatment of study drug with resolution of their illness but expired afterwards, this was also considered unrelated as clinical cure was documented and the death was not considered treatment failure. Study drug and death were considered related if there was treatment failure characterized by worsening of VABP that led to death after 48 hours of initiating treatment or if the subject's death was due to an AE related to the study treatment. There was one death related to an allergic reaction, presumably from the trial treatment in the HABP subgroup in a subject receiving linezolid/ceftazidime.
L1597: Based on the narrative reviews, the death and study drug relatedness were balanced between the two trial arms in the overall trial population with 12.6% of the deaths in the ceftobiprole arm and 14.3% of the deaths in the linezolid/ceftazidime arm deemed related to the study drug (Table 108). This balance in study drug relatedness is also seen within the subgroups. HABP subject deaths related to the trial treatment was seen in 17% of the ceftobiprole deaths and 16.7% linezolid/ceftazidime deaths. In the VABP subject subgroup, both treatment arms had 5.9% of the deaths deemed related to the Trial drug.
